author: Steakhouse
subject: A "send to stable" QoL ability
content_md:
The ability would need a prohibitively long cooldown (e.g. 1 hour) and work only out of combat.

To be clear, I'm not suggesting a remote "open the stable" as this would affect Hunter gameplay greatly, allowing them to swap pets between bosses, packs, battlegrounds, and even in the middle of fights via Feign Death (or just a Freezing trap in PvP), which isn't desirable.

I'm suggesting to add a send to stable ability for specifically two use cases :

 - You happen upon a beast you want to tame in the wild: it's rare, or it looks nice, or it's Brokentooth, or it has the latest rank of a pet spell you need. Currently you need to walk back to town, hope it has a stable master (or google it on wowhead, which breaks immersion), walk back, hope the mob is still there ... Or questing with a stabled pet and taming stuff on the go, which leads to hauling massive amounts of various foods. OR, already know everything you're gonna tame in advance, to know exactly when to stable your pet. IMO none of these scenarios are particularly desirable, giving a great niche to "send to stable" without altering balance in any way.

 - You want to tame 2 beasts in the same location, far from a Stable Master. Stable your main pet before you leave, tame the first pet, send to stable via ability, tame the second, dismiss or feed it.

author: Mosttrustworthy
subject: Re: Pet one button macro for hunters/
content_md:
Due to the volume of the desired functionality, it is necessary either to split the macro into two, or avail yourself of some macro-extending add-on.
I use SuperMacro, myself.

If Pet does not exist, Call Pet
Else if Pet is dead, Revive Pet
Else if Pet is in combat, Mend Pet
Else if Pet is the current target, Feed Pet with whatever is in the second slot of the first bag
Else Dismiss Pet
> /script local CSBN = CastSpellByName if not UnitExists("pet") then CSBN("Call Pet") elseif UnitIsDead("pet") then CSBN("Revive Pet") elseif UnitAffectingCombat("pet") then CBSN("Mend Pet") elseif UnitIsUnit("target", "pet") then CSBN("Feed Pet") PickupContainerItem(0, 2) else CSBN("Dismiss Pet") end

To select a different inventory slot to use with Feed Pet, change the numbers in PickupContainerItem(0, 2).
The game considers your bags to be your Containers, while your equipped gear is your Inventory.
Your bags go from 0 to 4, with 0 being the original backpack, getting further along the bag list as the number increases.
Inventory slots go from 1 to however many slots are in the specified bag.
Keep appropriate pet food in the same slot of the same bag and the macro will always work. Neglect this aspect of bag management and your pet might accidentally eat your Hearthstone.

Enabling mid-combat Dismissal requires an adjustment.

Etc.
If Pet is the current target, Dismiss Pet
Else if Pet is NOT in combat, Feed Pet
Else Mend Pet
> /script local CSBN = CastSpellByName if not UnitExists("pet") then CSBN("Call Pet") elseif UnitIsDead("pet") then CSBN("Revive Pet") elseif UnitIsUnit("pet") then CBSN("Dismiss Pet") elseif not UnitAffectingCombat("pet") then CSBN("Feed Pet") PickupContainerItem(0, 2) else CSBN("Mend Pet") end

author: Cochise
subject: Re: Working hunters mark mouseover macro?
content_md:
Code: Select all

```
/run local p,t,m,A="player","target","mouseover",UnitCanAttack local M=A(p,m)and not UnitIsUnit(t,m)if M then TargetUnit(m)end if A(p,t)then CastSpellByName"Hunter's Mark"end if M and UnitExists(t)then TargetLastTarget()end
```

Here's a breakdown of the macro
Code: Select all

```
/run
local p,t,m,A="player","target","mouseover",UnitCanAttack

-- Check if the mouseover unit is attackable and not the same as the target
local M=A(p,m)and not UnitIsUnit(t,m)

-- Target the mouseover unit if it's attackable
if M then TargetUnit(m)end

-- Cast "Hunter's Mark" on the current target if it's attackable
if A(p,t)then CastSpellByName"Hunter's Mark"end

-- Target the last target if changed
if M and UnitExists(t)then TargetLastTarget()end
```

author: Ragetto
subject: PvP Hunter > HUGE stealth nerf(s)?
content_md:
Hello,

I’m a regular PvP hunter, and I’ve been playing BGs daily for months.

Since this morning (post-server update), I’ve noticed several troubling issues with my hunter in BGs:

 1) Trap durations seem shorter (particularly Freezing Trap).
 2) Several "resists" on abilities that didn’t used to get resisted (or only in very specific contexts), such as Scatter Shot, Concussive Shot, etc.
 *(Need to confirm the second issue to assess the frequency.)*

I can guarantee with 99.9% certainty: changes have been made, and not minor ones, as they’ve completely disrupted some of my PvP routines (especially with Freezing Trap, where I have specific sequences that I can no longer execute—there’s simply not enough time). This has been tested on multiple opponents.

Before jumping to conclusions and making any decisions, I’d like to know if others have noticed these issues and whether it's a bug or a sneaky, stupid, yet impactful nerf.

 *PS: My spec is 30/21/0, so I don't have the talents to increase trap durations.*

Hello all.

Yes, a "change" was made -- a bugfix, as listed in the September 4 changelog here: [viewtopic.php?t=14765](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?t=14765)

This is a bugfix to behave blizzlike, as both in classic and vanilla those abilities shared DR.

If you would like to suggest that we change that, I encourage you to approach it that way, however large changes are coming to the Survival tree in the near future with our next patch, so they may not be long-lasting modifications.

Let this be a general warning not to let the thread further devolve into "turtle devs bad!" toxicity or punishments will be handed out accordingly.

author: Grizb37
subject: Re: PvP Hunter > HUGE stealth nerf(s)?
content_md:
Like said a popular pvp manuoveur for hunters is scatter shotting the target, feign death to drop combat, then place a trap and the scatter shotted target wanders into the trap. This is what any hunter with pvp skill does.

You can't just jump on a player feign death and ice trap, well you can, but any player that has any idea about pvp will just avoid the trap.

Conclusion

Because you need to use scatter and ice trap together to guarantee them landing in your ice trap, the duration of the latter will always be reduced significantly, this doesn't give the hunter enough time to get distance cast his mark then start an aimed shot or steady shot

author: Jstansberry
subject: Re: PvP Hunter > HUGE stealth nerf(s)?
content_md:
I know hunters aren't amazing in PvP when compared to some other classes, but tbh I welcome any change that nerfs casters/ranged damage in PvP. People often say that vanilla PvP has rock-paper-scissors balance i.e. class #1 handedly beats class #2 but is counterbalanced by losing handedly to class #3, while class #3 loses to #2 - but this is really not how it is at all. In reality, in small group, 1v1, or big battles like AV/AB, casters are king.

In large battles melee classes are basically just distractions/cannon fodder. Soul Link/Sacrifice warlock has a big advantage over everyone - yes, even against an ele shaman that presses Purge. Warriors lose to basically everyone in a 1v1, except maybe rogues - in group battles they are basically relegated to suicide charging to apply Mortal Strike debuff and Piercing Howl on a valuable target.

Vanilla PvP was never balanced in terms of how powerful each class is so IMO if the devs are choosing to push a blizzlike change on a very unblizzlike server project, it's just as justifiable as attempting to reshape vanilla PvP into something that even remotely resembles a balanced game. In my opinion, paladins becoming absolutely cracked because of Holy Strike being as overtuned as it is very vanilla-esque - not that I enjoy being critted for 6k holy damage Holy Strike+SoC in one swing but it definitely feels like it fits with all the other 2006 jank balance BS. If you wanna feel powerful in PvP, play a warlock, mage, paladin, ele shaman, or shadow priest.

subject: Survival Hunter tanking concept: talent changes
content_md:
Hello, I read on discord that Survival Hunter Tanking has been rejected but I am here to argue that it makes more sense for Survival to be a tank spec than it to be a melee dps spec.
On the other hand, I want to argue that Beast Mastery should be the melee dps focused spec but that post is in heavy making.

Why Hunter and Survival? Hunter because we need a pet class tank in the game and Survival because it has talents that just suit a tank well. It is called Survival after all.
Let's get over the talents that can be considered tank-like in the Survival tree:

 1) *Deflection*. It gives 5% more parry.
 2) *Survivalist*. Gives 10% more hp.
 3) *Deterrence*: Increases parry and dodge by 25% for 10 seconds.
 4) *Counterattack*: A strike that becomes active after you parry.
 5) *Lighting Reflexes*: Gives 15% agility.
 6) *Wyvern Sting*: A stinging shot that puts the target to sleep for 12 sec.

On the surface level these talents may seem mediocre but the tanking synergy is there; get into Aspect of the Monkey, put traps down before you pull. Use Multi-Shot or Wyvern Sting depending if you want more threat or to play it safe. When the mobs come to attack you, increase your avoidances with Deterrence to enable the use of Counterattack and Mongoose Bite. Strike them down with your 2h using Raptor Strike making both your defenses and offenses shine during this tank dance. And if you lose threat on a mob, then taunt with your pet or use distracting shot if you're far away. Feign Death if a dps pulls the mobs first.

But I did not include the dps enhancing talents even tho they contribute a lot to tanks. Even parry by itself would greatly reduce the speed of your next auto attack, making your Raptor Strike that much smoother to use. Therefore I suspect a 2h would be the best use for this tanking style, even without any talent support. **I am not saying Survival tanking doesn't have its problems, far from it; all I am saying is that it makes sense from the right perspective.**

Either way you see at Survival Tanking, I want to show you my take on how to rework the Survival talent tree to make it more tank-like, with melee ideas in mind, but also not crazy anti-blizz-like.

content_md:
I disagree here (agreeing with Bigsmerf).
Besides the improved predator aspects (where aspect of the wolf was added by TWOW) and maybe the improved aspect of the monkey buff nothing in the BM tree supports melee.
However, survival does: superior strikes, savage strikes, improved slaying, deterrence, counterattack etc.
BM by design has to remain a 'puppeteer' tree where you mostly fight with your pet, supporting it from behind. I wish TWOW made them relevant for raids, though, I'd love to see some hunters mostly relying on pet damage at raids (if this doesn't break PVP).
MM is without a question a ranged build.
Survival... Survival is weird. You can ask many hunters and each will give a different asnwer.
Survival tree can be:
 * A random utility 'shop' where you go in to buy some cool talents for your ranged hunter.
 * A utility tree (better traps, feign death, even wyvern sting) which needs some push like in-combat traps to make a full-utility hunter build running around, setting up traps, kiting etc.
 * A melee tree.
 * The skeleton of a tanking tree.

As far as I see, the tree was designed for single-leveling and PVP. Mongoose bite and counterattack can indeed only trigger if you dodge or parry but the team back in the day didn't give enough survivability (pun intended) to the hunter to make it ready to tank. Not even threat modifiers except for that one shot I can't remember the name of.
Originally the tree was designed for a player who roams the land, farms mobs for quest and maybe does some world PVP.
This can be changed to a tank build (I wouldn't be against it) but many people would riot, saying it's not Vanilla+ anymore, it's SoD (remember how 90% of the people booed the healer mage idea there).
I'm pretty sure that TWOW will do something with the tree but it will probably get one role and more people want melee DPS as a hunter than to tank with them.
Dru's feral tree and shaman's enh tree are different. In case of the dru, Blizzard back in the day wasn't sure how to allow 4 playstyles via 3 talent trees so they made feral tree a melee DPS + tanking tree. Allowing each playstyles for dru was the dru's core identity via shapeshifting.
In case of the shaman, there is a huge playerbase wanting to melee DPS as enh and a lot of other guys wanting to shaman tank. It's also better explicable flavor-wise, shamans were the 'almost tanks' of Vanilla.
In case of hunter, a lot of people wanna melee DPS as a hunter and I'm pretty sure, TWOW will enable that playstyle with the patch. But there's just not enough playerbase wanting the hunter tank to make survival a melee+tank tree just like enh shaman tree.
Also, flavorwise it's weird. Shamans already have an ásspull to explain why their mitigation should be at least comparable to plate-wearing palas (+30% armor from shield custom talent).
With hunters you'd have to explain why a guy with mail and without any shield should have a comparable mitigation.

author: Eeeeeeeeeee
subject: Re: Survival Hunter tanking concept: talent changes
content_md:
I've actually been leveling a Tank Hunter (face, not pet) and for dungeoning it already works ok and the playstyle is very fun. Big proponent of some improvements to the style, and I think talents are one area that can be done. These are some cool ideas, and I appreciate that you kept an eye to most of the talents being a bit agnostic -- the trap talents are just as good for any utility focused Hunter as a Tank Hunter, for instance. It takes a bit more community approval for such changes I think, but likely has the best results in the end.

In my experience, a big part of what makes Tank Hunter fun to play is the high amount of juggling involved. Imo it's one of the most demanding playstyles for leveling, because to play it well you have to micro two characters and for one of them the positioning is very tight.

Tank Hunter as it stands involves a triple-single target style of:
- Shooting ranged enemies, or melees held by your pet, with autos, Distracting, and Multishot

- Meleeing melee enemies with autos Raptors, Mongoose, Counterattack, and sometimes Wing Clip

- Controlling the position of ranged/melee enemies so Multishot can hit all 3 targets

- Microing your pet to ensure good Screech coverage and to hold certain enemies for you

- Pre-fight trapping for control/aggro

- Moving *away* from aggro pullers on your team to be able to re-establish aggro

- Occasionally popping a defensive CD
Tl;dr you're doing melee, ranged, and pet control all at the same time.

With that in mind, I think furthering the distinction in the style is a good thing and it's power can go up some without anyone's normal conception of the gaming changing much. I would, however, keep an eye on the PVP crowd here as I doubt they'd want Hunter suddenly becoming super tanky.

To that end, I like your changes to Counterattack and Deterrence. Dodge/parry area big part of Tank Hunter, so encouraging it feels right and the melee threat is needed. I would also allow Counterattack/Mongoose some scaling as well since their damage is incredibly low.

Bonus threat on the traps is good, tho I might be happier with "Multi-shot now applies Distracting Shot." This reinforces the triple-single style we currently have and still doesn't sound like something any DPS Hunter would want. That idea is a little more wacky tho.

From a tanking perspective, I also like the need for pets to have some aggro in order to enable mid-combat traps. It's nice and reinforces the pet as a part of your tanking. Non-tank Hunters can still use Feign Death as always.

I'd say keep an eye on the Improve Ice/Fire Traps, as they seem very strong and more generically useful. I'm not against a more utility focus tho, so I'd want to see how that shook out.

The part I'm most iffy about is the Beast Mastery changes, as its quite a bit of tankiness available to any spec. In PvE I imagine this wouldn't make too big a difference, but it is a pretty general Hunter buff. In PvP I bet people would be annoyed. I'd like to see a touch more tankiness, but maybe just not in this form.

Overall I like it and I'd be happy to see it go in as is, tho I'd want the team to keep an eye on the BM and Improves Traps ones.

Lastly, I'd also like to test another idea in Hunter tanking as well:
- Improved Cower: Your pet's cower now transfers their aggro on the target to you instead of removing it.
The hope here is that, combined with the incentive to have mobs attack your pet, you can sometimes have your pet holding aggro and sometimes have them helping you hold it. Lots of good micro potential there and a versatile tool for control in fights. The worry is that it may be too much aggro gen when combined with other changes. Still, I'd like to see it tried. The other worry is that it may make pet pulling even better in raids, dunno if people would be upset about that or not. Add a distance-to-Hunter limit if that is an issue.

There's lots of additional ways you could refine the vision, like having Mongoose Bite cause aggro for your pet, encouraging aggro juggling between the two of you. Or giving one of your melee abilities a chance to refresh Distracting Shot. Or having your pet gain some focus when aggro swaps away from them. I think the room is definitely there for this to be a unique tanking style while feeling properly Vanilla+.

Anyway I'd love to see a bit more support for tank Hunter, absolutely on board, and personally I also don't mind the buffs not being super powerful. Enough to make it work well for those that want to, not enough to define the meta.

author: Cochise
subject: Re: IsAutoRepeatAction() is bugged - cannot make spammable Auto Shot Macro
content_md:
> **Bashor wrote: Thu Sep 26, 2024 12:57 am**
> I checked it again and using only the Auto Shot line as demonstrated in your video does work perfectly. The first line in the following macro clearly works, however the second one will now cause the attack animation to be spammed in a similar fashion to not using a macro at all.
>
>  /run if TargetUnit("player")==nil or TargetUnit("player")==friend then TargetNearestEnemy()end
>  /run if not IsAutoRepeatAction(36)then CastSpellByName("Auto Shot")end

The issue is your macro. TargetUnit doesn't return a value; it only targets a unit. Thus, you're targeting yourself before switching to the nearest enemy, which interrupts Auto Shot. To get those values, use functions UnitExists and UnitIsFriend.

Here's a working version
Code: Select all

```
/run if not UnitCanAttack("player","target")then TargetNearestEnemy()end if not IsAutoRepeatAction(36)then CastSpellByName"Auto Shot"end
```

Here's a working version

/run if not UnitCanAttack("player","target")then TargetNearestEnemy()end if not IsAutoRepeatAction(36)then CastSpellByName"Auto Shot"end

author: Silhouette
subject: Hunter QoL Improvements
content_md:
Hello fellows hunters and Turtle devs,

Throughout my journey on Turtle WoW, I've been thinking about what could make things better for hunters while keeping a Vanilla logic, so after having done some research (also on the Forum so I don't repeat the idea of someone else), a few ideas came to my mind:

 **Ammos QoL**

 - Adding Green Arrows crafts within the Survivalist profession, so Engineering would not be the only way to craft ammos and being able to make these with a secondary job would make things more accessible.
 - Implementing a counterpart NPC in order to trade Survivalist Arrows for Bullets equivalent, just like the Thorium Shells to trade for Thorium Headed Arrows in OG/IF.
 - Adding Blue ammos to craft, in the form of a rare schematic (or survivalist plans) for example inside the loot table of a new raid or already existing one like the Schematic: Biznicks 247x128 Accurascope obtainable in Molten Core.

 **Quiver and Bandolier QoL**

 - Adding an epic Bandolier equivalent to the Ancient Sinew Wrapped Lamina (from the Rhok'delar questline), maybe obtainable through a new Hunter questline or simply as a new drop.
 - Making Quiver and Bandolier as an independent slot so it doesn't sacrifice one inventory slot. I've heard, an extra stable slot is going to be available within the Turtle Shop in an upcoming update, so maybe could this extra Quiver/Bandolier slot be sold within the Shop too ?
 - Since Quivers have different skins visible on the back of our character, sometimes it just doesn't fit with the Xmog of the character so adding an Illusion or a way to Xmog the Quiver would be great for fashionistas!

Thank you for your time, hope that some of you guys like these ideas!  smiling_turtle

subject: Another CRYMORE Hunter thread.
content_md:
Hi. And yes, feel free to say it's deserved and blablabla. I made a thread just to summ up all my dissapointment in upcoming CC2 as a PVP hunter.

Lets start.
 1. Wing Clip is a meme now. Making it 6 sec cd is just worst decision. It will affect not only pvp aspect but pve too.
I just fought a warrior and he just dodged wing clip 3 times in a row, as a result im dead. Imagine it has 6 sec cd and not landing it will cut off many 1 v 1 scenarios for a hunter in pvp. In pve now u cant just wing clip 3 - 4 mobs and kite them without trap. + I have no clue how Rokdelar quest is going to be done now without normal wing clip. 1 parry or Dodge may result drama. Just please leave it alone...

 2. You just deleted Counterattack and i dont understand a reason to do that at all lol. It was the main source in pvp to fight VS Rogues and Warriors to break the distance a bit and make couple of shots or trinket hamstring/poison and try to escape. In fact it could only be triggered when dodge/parry. But the best part of it you just gave it to a warriors instead, and now when we hunters will pop Deterrence we pretty much dead vs warrior. Great design. Not to mention it was the HUNTER EXCLUSIVE talent/ability made of purpose by Blizzard for our class to survive.

 3. The idea of putting Trap Mastery into 5th row is just BAD DESIGN. The whole Talent trees right now are forcing you to play deep into that tree cutting off all other aspect of hybrid. Without this talent the traps are going to be resisted here and there, which simply will make usage of them almost pointless in other trees. I just played BG and a paladin resisted 2 out of 3 traps without trap mastery lol.

 4. Viper Sting. Okay it might be discussed. You took away and ability to suppress enemy backline of healers/casters completely at this point, but anyway in good teams it was almost instantly dispelled BUT it was forcing enemy healers to waste a GCD to dispell it. Now its just whatever ability and i don't see much potential in it unless you do it physical debuff which cannot be dispelled, with yeah 6sec cd, that will be fair at least. But making it 6 sec and lowering the values with an ability of dispelling it by almost every class in game is just a meme.

 5. Savage Strikes talent changes was not necessary at all, i would prefer old version of it with 20%+ crit chance on raptor strike, for both pve and pvp. Not its just 6% to all Melee ability.

 6. Loghtning Reflexes got donwgraded to 10% agility and transfering agility into Melee AP. I mean, well its designed now for Melee hunter, not much to cry about, i just suggest to leave it as it was 15% and make less transfer to melee AP, so both melee hunter and ranged hybrid/mm would benefit from that.

Reading hunters section in discord is just pure depression now. I hope you guys roll back all this stuff and dont make a hunter pure backline class in pvp cutting off 1 v 1 aspect (at least with melees). For now i only see it MM Build is mandatory, and still even in MM build you cant reach TRAP MASTERY so again traps are very questionable.

You already 'fixed' Scatter/trap combo some time ago, which already made pvp worse but everything above will just ruin it completely.

Overall it feels very bad to see all other classes getting buffed huge in both pvp/pve aspects such as holy/prot palas (im not talking about rets at this point), disc priests(they are seems unkillable holy smite pumpers now lol), mages, druids... And hunters just a pure pve buff. Please.

P.S. The mobility and ability to KITE as a hunter was the core aspect of the class in both pvp/pve aspects. It was like identity. And now im not sure who i am lol.

Same for Hamstring for warrior. In the 20~ years wow has existed, warriors have always had Hamstring and it never once in that time ever got given a CD. The change to both wing clip and hamstring were wholly unnecessary. If it had ever been a problem, it would have been changed on Blizzard servers as well at some point.

author: Ragetto
subject: Re: Another CRYMORE Hunter thread.
content_md:
I completely agree with everything that Diablo has said. Due to the 'melee' tree (seriously, wtf), PvP hunters are becoming absolutely disastrous: they’re shifting from a class with a very high skill cap (which was already lowered with the recent scatter/trap nerf) to a class for backpedalers who are perfectly fine just shooting from a distance and racking up big numbers (to chill after a PvE raid where they did, well... exactly the same) while getting crushed by the first rogue or warrior they encounter. But for that kind of players, it doesn’t change much, as that’s always been the case.

The survival tree should be an utility tree, not a melee tree... I don't understand why devs would destroy the very essence of a class to cater to a small minority obsessed with a meme spec.

 *Even though fewer hunters may care, I also plan to make a specific post about the BM/MM PvP hunter (30-21-0: very fun build with stun and scatter) that, on top of the nerfs to Viper Sting and Wing Clip, is facing a drastic reduction in DPS... with absolutely NOTHING in return. While this build is far from overpowered, it’s just fun as long as it’s somewhat effective.*

Honestly, because of the 'melee' tree (which should have remained a joke among hunters), the devs have killed all other viable playstyles, which are the essence of the class.

Now we’re left with the choice between turret DPS without mobility and... a melee class (seriously, wtf again). I thought I’d seen the worst after the scatter/trap nerf, but I was light-years away from imagining what awaited us.

author: Juzam
subject: Re: Another CRYMORE Hunter thread.
content_md:
While everything seems fine for PVE, the current ranged physical damage pvp build was completely destroyed.

What hunter needed the most is ways to regain distance, especially against mages (removing deadzone or wotlk disengage would have solved the issue), but they went the opposite direction and nerfed the few clunky ways we got.

I still cannot explain how they could think it was a good idea to remove counterattack, or to put a CD on wingclip (or harmstring), they even removed the talent to reduce trap being resisted from early survival making traps unreliable for other specs.

Hunter was already on the lowest tier of the performing classes for PVP (as well as warriors) and they nerfed us even further.

On the other hand, they added extra damage to Crits with piercing shots (who can break traps by the way) while hunter is already the class who benefit the most from crits and added a free attack proc with endless quivers. Because of that, when stars align, it will cause massive burst damage and people will still complain about us.

While there is plenty of choices if you want to be a melee or a caster, there is only one to be a physical ranged damage dealer, please revert those changes for those who like pvp as physical ranged.

It's too bad because there is very good changes in this patch but unfortunately, some very badly tought changes curently ruin it.

They should definitely make an open test realm for everyone to test and comment on that patch because currently the class council proven to have massive flaw / lack of understanding of how the game work / or 0 care of the PVP side / to even think about removing counterattack / adding a CD on harmstring / wingclip.

author: Ragetto
subject: Re: Another CRYMORE Hunter thread.
content_md:
> **Scelus12 wrote: Fri Oct 18, 2024 5:14 pm**
> What exactly was the reason behind the wing clip nerf?

Long story short:
> Survival tree is now a 90% melee tree (wtf, but... yeah)
> Melee = windfury proc triggered by wing clip
> Windfury proc = too much DPS in pve
> Nerf wing clip (instead of limiting the proc itself)

In other words, because of melee huntards, pvp hunters are being penalized. But honestly, this is just one issue among many. The only tree that hasn't changed much is Beast Mastery, and the changes there are actually interesting (because the pet's stats finally scale based on the hunter's stats).

> **Scelus12 wrote: Fri Oct 18, 2024 5:14 pm**
> Why/how is Scatter/trap nerfed?

Freezing Trap and Scatter Shot now share the same diminishing returns, and have for the past two months... So when you use Trap after Scatter, it lasts a very short time. Shorter than it did in vanilla, but they'll never admit that.

Funny thing is, it was supposed to be a "blizz-like" bug fix...

> **Scelus12 wrote: Fri Oct 18, 2024 5:14 pm**
> Those both seem like absolutely essential tools for PvP, and given hunter was underperforming, I don't see the logic in it.

author: Dyco

content_md:
I've seen several comments complaining about the changes announced for the hunter in patch 1.17.2, specificlly those related to survival tree. People seems to forget that survival tree was originally designed to be melee ([https://web.archive.org/web/20041210202 ... lect_id=11](https://web.archive.org/web/20041210202226/http://wowvault.ign.com/View.php?view=Talents.View&category_select_id=11)).
I must say that I agree with most of the changes announced, but disagree with some others.
Specifically regarding the performance that the hunter could have in pvp, there would be things that I would consider reversing.

My suggestions are as follows:

keep Counterattack
keep Wing Clip as it is right now (no weapon scaling, no 6sec cooldown).
Reeplace 1.17.2 announced Wing Clip with a new melee strike, old pre-1.12.1 hunter's Lacerate (no bleeding, just weapon scaling and 6 sec cooldown).
Add an a Tranquilizing Shot equivalent strike for melee hunters (no weapon damage, same cooldown).
Merge all actual Trap talents into one.

That been said, my suggestion for survival tree would be this:

 --1st row--

 * **IMPROVED SLAYING**: (3 points) (just as it's right now).
 * **RESOURCEFULNESS**: (5 points) (just as announced in 1.17.2).
 * **DEFLECTION**: (2 points) (just as announced in 1.17.2).

 --2nd row--

 * **TRAP MASTERY**: (3 points) *Increases the duration of Freezing and Frost Trap by 10/20/30% and the damage of Inmolation and Explosive Trap by 10/20/30%. Also gives your traps a 8/16/25% chance to entrap the target preventing them to move for 5 sec and decreases the chance enemies will resist trap effects by 5/10/15%.*
 * **SAVAGE STRIKES**: (2 points) (as announced in 1.17.2).
 * **IMPROVED WING CLIP**: (3 points) (as announced in 1.17.2).
 * **SURVIVAL INSTINCTS**: (2 points) (merge of old pre-1.12.1 Improved Disengage and actual Improved Feign Death) *Reduces the chance your Feign Death ability will be resisted by 2/4%. Increases the amount of threat reduced by your Disengange ability by 10/20%.*

 --3rd row--

 * **PLANNING AHEAD**: (2 points) (requires 3 points in Trap Mastery) (juast as announced in 1.17.2).
 * **SURVIVALIST**: (5 points) (just as it's right now).
 * **CARVE**: (1 point) (just as announced in 1.17.2).
 * **DETERRANCE**: (1 point) (just as it's right now).

 --4th row--

 * **STINGING NETTLE LACING**: (2 points) (just as announced in 1.17.2).
 * **SUREFOOTED**: (3 points) (just as it's right now).
 * **COUNTERATTACK**: (1 point) (requires 1 point in Deterrance) (just as it's right now).

 --5th row--

 * **KILLER INSTINCT**: (3 points) (just as announced in 1.17.2).
 * **MELEE SPECIALIZATION**: (5 points) (old pre-1.12.1 talent) *Increases the damage you deal with melee weapons by 1/2/3/4/5%.*
 * **RAPID STRIKES**: (1 point) (requires 1 talent point in Carve) (just as announced in 1.17.2).

 --6th row--

 * **LACERATE**: (1 point) (requires 3 points in Killer Instinct) (old pre-1.12.1 talent without bleeding effect) *An instant strike that deals 40% weapon damage increased by 45% of your Attack Power.*
 * **LIGHTING REFLEXES**: (3 points) (as announced in 1.17.2, but with 3 talent points) *Increases your Agility by 3/6/10% and increases your attack power by an amount equal to 30/65/100% of your agility.*
 * **VICIOUS BITE**: (2 points) (just as announced in 1.17.2).

 --7th row--

 * **UNTAMED TRAPPER**: (1 point) (as announced in 1.17.2 but without being linked to Trap Mastery).

Total points: 51

This is how it would look like:
[embed: https://s9e.github.io/iframe/2/imgur.min.html#Br8io2j]

subject: Re: Another CRYMORE Hunter thread.
content_md:
There is a screenshot of notes taken from the stream of Vrograg which includes changes to the patch note.

![Image](https://media.discordapp.net/attachments/810850727215104050/1297732948073648228/image.png?ex=6716ff7d&is=6715adfd&hm=50174b214f2798b1672034ffc12888d87ff3f09893723ed1c37b77451d3469ed&=&format=webp&quality=lossless&width=469&height=468)

Wing Clip getting a 3 sec CD rather than 6 is far better. We lose 1 Wing Clip with the GCD compared to spamming, but Improved Clip now go to 40% change to root the target ! To be fair, for the old playstyle of ranged hunters, I find it rather balanced (and necessary with the loss of Counter Attack and the need to be able to root enough against rogues or warriors). I just fear it will be nerfed because for an offensive melee hunter, 40% chance to root your target is quiiiiite violent.

With that change, compared to vanilla, we still have the nerf of Scatter Shot/Freeze Trap DR, Trap Mastery is too far so 4-5% chance the target resist our traps, no Counter Attack, Raptor Strike burst much less happening. But we get more damage in BM or MM.

I don't know if it's enough, as I prefer (and the hunter needs it) many mobility/abilities to kite. We still lost some. But the increase in damage could maybe compensate the need to kite so much. I'm not sure. Seems a little better than before, hope it's enough.

As for Shadowmeld, in Night Elf, continuing to cry. Usually, you could open with an Aimed Shot without problem, so it's just a bigger CD and I don't care for the 2 sec of stealth. But I'm still curious to see how it could work.

content_md:
I came to these forums after a frustrating few days grinding PvP.  Currently I think to myself, why play Hunter? If you want to win as a ranged DPS now just roll priest, warlock or druid.

I definitely have room to improve as a player,  but in summary  I feel a tad fed up with becoming useless every time a player decides to charge at me, I just have no answer to it.

author: Ragetto
subject: Re: Another CRYMORE Hunter thread.
content_md:
I mostly play my priest now, but I recently tried my R13 hunter with a 30/21/0 spec (stun + scatter shot). It used to be a niche but viable build, and now I think it’s the best pvp spec for hunters. Honestly, it might be the only truly viable one left, so... I’d recommend giving it a shot. It’s still strong (maybe stronger than before) and, in my opinion, really fun to play.

Sadly, the classic 0/30/21 hunter spec is dead. It’s basically the same as before, just worse in every single aspect.

On top of that, Freezing Trap can now be broken with the pvp trinket, which is a huge nerf for hunters. Setting traps already had so many limitations compared to spammable cc like sheep/fear... Seems like the devs understand pvp even less than I thought.

Sad thing is, most of the pre-1.17.1 pvp hunters I used to fight with/against (some of whom were already hunter mains back in 2004) are gone. They’ve either rerolled or quit twow. Only a handful of new hunters remain, and they’re not experienced enough to understand what has actually happened.

That said, vanilla feels far away now, but before you reroll or give up on twow, I’d recommend trying the 30/21/0 spec. It’s strong and fun, even if it doesn’t feel like the classic hunter you used to love.

content_md:
The 30/21/0 build I use:
[https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/hunter?p ... AAAAAAA%3D](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/hunter?points=FYACBoAoJCQYAAFACoQBAoIAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA%3D)

This spec took the same nerfs as the others (Viper Sting, Wing Clip, Freezing Trap), but it was a bit less reliant on the nerfed abilities (+ we didn’t have Counterattack).

The pet hits a bit harder now, even though I had to drop 2 points from Frenzy. And what’s also interesting is Swift Aspect - it procs a lot. From what I understand, the rework nerfed it in PvE, but in PvP, it’s clearly a buff (I didn’t even have this talent before 1.17.2).

author: Ragetto
subject: 1.17.2 - PvP Hunter > Please Save the BM/MM Spec 🙏
content_md:
Hello,

 ----------------- edit -----------------
Great news: according to the talent simulator, Hawk Eye has been moved back to Tier 3 in the MM tree (swapped with Improved Hunter's Mark), which means it no longer competes with Mortal Shots.
 -------------------------------------------

 *A comprehensive post has already been created regarding the general impact on PvP hunters (Viper Sting, Wing Clip), and more specifically on the "classic" PvP hunter (so far MM/Survival 0/21/30 - which, in 1.17.2, will become a stationary DPS turret in deep MM).*
 *edit: [viewtopic.php?f=45&t=15234](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?f=45&t=15234)*

As for me, I want to advocate for a spec that's a bit less common, but one of the most fun in the game across all classes, reasonably viable until now (especially useful for under-geared hunters, but it works for everyone), yet it’s being completely destroyed by the 1.17.2 update (and the MM tree restructuring), making it no longer viable. This reduces the diversity of the hunter class and the game itself.

I’m talking about the hybrid Beast Mastery/Marksmanship spec (30/21/0), which allows you to have both the pet stun and Scatter Shot. Not viable for PvE raiding, of course, but incredibly fun in PvP, with plenty of little tricks (resulting in a high skill cap) and decent dps...
[https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/c ... 0000000000](https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/calculator/custom?t1=R21loaF9Ag&t0=MPGOMWitwz&t2=nC2KvPaEKT&t=0150003221500050010000500000-0500005011030050100000000000-0000000000000000000000000000)

More broadly, what I’m going to describe applies to all specs that invest 21 points into MM to obtain Scatter Shot. You’ll see how the restructuring of the MM tree results in a significant DPS (or range) nerf compared to before.

 *Note: I’m speaking as an experienced PvP hunter who has played this class at a high level in Vanilla, TBC, WotLK, and achieved (almost) everything possible in PvP. Now on Twow, I’ve reached Rank 13, though I'm aware that rank itself only reflects time spent, not actual skill. Anyway, I just wanted to clarify that I’m not an RP backpedaler advocating for a meme spec... nothing more.*

Here is the new BM/MM build as it would be in 1.17.2:
[https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/hunter?p ... AAAAAAA%3D](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/hunter?points=AoAaBoAoRBAoAAFAEoABQYIAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA%3D)

There aren’t major differences in the BM tree (more armor and HP for the pet, which can be useful in very specific situations but overall... who cares), so I won’t go into it here.

 --------------------------------
Looking at the 1.17.2 Marksmanship tree, you quickly realize that something is off..

 **Tier 1** ![✅](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/2705.svg)
OK

 **Tier 2** ![✅](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/2705.svg)
OK

 **Tier 3** ![⚠️](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/26a0.svg)
Steady Shot makes its appearance, okay, fair enough... But wait, where’s Hawk Eye?
Now I’m "forced" to spend my points in Improved Stings (which only serves to compensate for the base nerf).

 **Tier 4** ![⚠️](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/26a0.svg)![🔥](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/1f525.svg)![🔥](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/1f525.svg)![🔥](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/1f525.svg)![⚠️](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/26a0.svg)
Oh, here’s Hawk Eye! But what’s it doing here?
It’s now competing with Mortal Shots... I only have 5 points, but I need 7 to get back to my previous level of effectiveness.
What should I choose? Range or damage?
This "choice" didn’t exist before, it’s a massive nerf, plain and simple.

 --------------------------------

So, to summarize, as a BM/MM:

 **What’s worse:**

- Wing Clip cooldown (applies to all hunters)

- Viper Sting cooldown and nerf (applies to all hunters)

- My damage and/or range (in short, a huge sacrifice)

 **What’s better:**

- 2 more stable slots (applies to all hunters)

- Uh… that’s it   sad_turtle

Basically, as a BM/MM hunter, I just become weaker with NO compensation. At all (not even in the BM tree since I don’t go deep enough).

It’s both unexpected and depressing.

 --------------------------------

The strength of the original design was that you could play multiple specs with different playstyles, but that will no longer be possible (I don’t count the melee spec, which doesn’t really exist in my mind). Gameplay is one thing, but fun only exists when there’s a reasonable level of effectiveness, and with so many nerfs, the BM/MM spec is no longer viable for serious PvP play.

So, dear Turtle WoW team, I beg you: don’t kill such a fun spec.

Please modify your future MM tree so that it’s still possible, with 21 points in MM, to have Hawk Eye AND 5/5 Mortal Shots. I’m not asking for any improvements or buffs, just to be able to keep playing this spec.

Please don’t make your game less fun and diverse than the original.

author: Ishilu
subject: Don't replace the survival tree with a melee tree
content_md:
Simple as that.

Survival in its current for is for snaring and CC'ing with melee skills just being escape tools.

The announced class changes replace this playstyle with a pure melee dps spec.

If you want to give the Rexxar melee hunter crowd some fun, well, go for it, but please don't do so at the expense of people who enjoy the classic hunter playstyle. So, dear devs, please go ahead and keep adding content and playstyles to the game but please don't remove stuff.

My suggestion to make more people happy would be to either
a) just add a fourth talent tree for melee hunters
or
b) simply make one talent tree wider (by the way, why not BM? You know... Rexxar) so that people can choose to either enhance their melee dps or stay true a ranged hunter spec. This could be done with talent dependencies so players would have to choose their path within the tree.

I'm pretty sure melee hunters can be added to the game without removing survival hunters.

keep Counterattack
keep Wing Clip as it is right now (no weapon scaling, no 6sec cooldown).

Merge all actual Trap talents into one.

 --1st row--

 * **IMPROVED SLAYING**: (3 points) (just as it's right now).

 --2nd row--

 * **TRAP MASTERY**: (3 points) *Increases the duration of Freezing and Frost Trap by 10/20/30% and the damage of Inmolation and Explosive Trap by 10/20/30%. Also gives your traps a 8/16/25% chance to entrap the target preventing them to move for 5 sec and decreases the chance enemies will resist trap effects by 5/10/15%.*
 * **SAVAGE STRIKES**: (2 points) (as announced in 1.17.2).
 * **IMPROVED WING CLIP**: (3 points) (as announced in 1.17.2).

 --3rd row--

 * **CARVE**: (1 point) (just as announced in 1.17.2).
 * **DETERRANCE**: (1 point) (just as it's right now).

 --4th row--

 * **STINGING NETTLE LACING**: (2 points) (just as announced in 1.17.2).
 * **SUREFOOTED**: (3 points) (just as it's right now).
 * **COUNTERATTACK**: (1 point) (requires 1 point in Deterrance) (just as it's right now).

 --5th row--

 * **KILLER INSTINCT**: (3 points) (just as announced in 1.17.2).
 * **MELEE SPECIALIZATION**: (5 points) (old pre-1.12.1 talent) *Increases the damage you deal with melee weapons by 1/2/3/4/5%.*
 * **RAPID STRIKES**: (1 point) (requires 1 talent point in Carve) (just as announced in 1.17.2).

 --6th row--

 * **LACERATE**: (1 point) (requires 3 points in Killer Instinct) (old pre-1.12.1 talent without bleeding effect) *An instant strike that deals 40% weapon damage increased by 45% of your Attack Power.*
 * **LIGHTING REFLEXES**: (3 points) (as announced in 1.17.2, but with 3 talent points) *Increases your Agility by 3/6/10% and increases your attack power by an amount equal to 30/65/100% of your agility.*

author: Azuredrak0
subject: Re: Don't replace the survival tree with a melee tree
content_md:
There's nothing preventing people from playing the same way they do today - trapping and snaring - with current implementation of the Survival tree.  The only thing that's missing is Counterattack (which is unreliable and very short duration) and on top of that 1.17.2 survival also adds traps in combat, and melee viability.

The way I see this spec being played in PvP is not necessarily by rushing into melee, but rather, still working down the opponent from range until that opponent insists on closing into melee, at which point you have a choice of Freezing Trap and do the same thing again, or stand your ground, pop cooldowns, and rip his face off...

I also believe that this spec is going to be nerfed, as placing a Freezing trap down in melee - you can do this forever in combat without 30 second Feign Death restriction.

author: therealrexxar
subject: Mongoose Bite and what it means to be a "Melee Hunter"
content_md:
Ahhh, "melee hunter", our favorite meme spec. The moment we have been so patiently waiting for has finally come...

But first let's make sure it's done properly. This new topic won't raise the issues that the other topic has raised as that would be unnecessary, even though I agree with most points, especially giving us back Counterattack and the Wing Clip CD being reduced.

I think more changes should be made to make everyone happy. I have some suggestions:
 1.1) Change Mongoose Bite to make it require dodge again.
 1.2) Add/change a talent to allow MB to be usable without having to dodge. Perhaps by using an already existing 1-pointer talent from the Survival Tree (Rapid Strikes seems to be the best option imo).
Justification:
Changing MB to require dodge again might not be the most popular suggestion as it's not very convenient but I think it's necessary not only for the Hunter class as a whole but also for the melee hunter archetype. This way you can still use MB if you want to go deep Survival (which you will want to do anyway as you need the new Vicious Bite to make it worth using). This change would mean many things:
a) From a PvP standpoint, it will allow to separate the specs more, helping a bit with the nightmare of balancing ranged vs melee hunter in the future. MM and BM hunter can stay the same while the Vicious Bite talent (*) allows it to be used for Survival, with adjustments to the talent if necessary allowing MB to be balanced much more easily. Everyone is happy.
 * (great talent btw, 10/10. And it is very similar to the beta talent "Improved Mongoose Bite" as a bonus. Sometimes simple is better)
b) It will allow for more freedom of choice between specs, including for hybrids (more on that in my 2nd suggestion). Choosing to be a melee hunter vs ranged hunter should not be as linear as going Survival vs MM (or BM if you rely more heavily on pets). BM should also be an option for melee hunters. We all know Rexxar is a Beastmaster, not a Survival Hunter.
c) From a PvE standpoint, it doesn't really make much difference except BM melee hunters won't use it. However, as I said before, it won't be worth using without deep Survival talents anyway. Also, you won't be able to use it while leveling until you pick 21 talents tree in the Survival tree, which might not make leveling as melee as interactive, but in return, you will be able to focus on other talents in the meantime.
d) Conceptually (last but not least), it doesn't make sense for MB to be usable without dodging. The theme around that ability is to counterattack (speaking of which, please give us Counterattack back   scared_turtle_head  ) swiftly after dodging, just as mongooses do in real life. Allowing MB to be usable all the time by picking the Rapid Strikes talent seems to be a good option to me and keeps the flavor of the ability.

 2) Change the Killer Instinct and Lightning Reflexes talents. Both talents are deep in the Survival Tree and they should feel less mandatory for playing melee hunter.
Justification:
I'm sure most players think of Rexxar as the prime example of what a melee hunter is. It should come as no surprise to many that Rexxar, the archetype of melee hunter, is a Beastmaster in WC3. I believe that these changes are forcing us choose between one and another, which personally I think it's unfair. One should be able to be a beastmaster and still play as a melee hunter, they should not be mutually exclusive.
However, I feel that currently devs seem to be aiming for BM to be the "ranged but stronger pet" tree since, the way things are right now, playing as ranged will always feel much more powerful than melee if you go the Bestial Wrath route, even if you pick talents that buff your melee abilities in the Survival Tree as the remaining talents. Choosing Bestial Wrath means not being able to choose both Killer Instinct and Lightning Reflexes (both deep in the Survival Tree), which feel mandatory for melee with the way things are right now as they provide the necessary scaling for melee to be viable.
I believe that the new Survival tree needs a better arrangement. Deep Survival shouldn't be so tied to melee damage and the whole tree should have its damage better distributed among the rows. Otherwise, melee will always suck as BM. This tree makes it impossible for BMs to melee as well.
And before you think that this new tree is how it was intended to be based on the beta Survival Tree (pre-1.12), I'll just say it's not. The beta Survival tree did not have such mandatory talents like the two mentioned above. So it's not even close. Some of them were good but none of them were required. And that is what this discussion is all about. I am all for more talents for support the melee playstyle, in fact I advertise often in the discord channel for it and even used the beta Survival Tree before as an argument for more melee support.

Thank you devs for listening to us.   satisfied_turtle

author: Juzam
subject: @Devs 1.17.2 : Impact on Hunter class / why haste is good
content_md:
Hi devs, first of all, thanks for the amazing work you did with Twow.

Before reviewing the changes, a "quick" presentation : I'm Focus, a hunter in the best PVE guild on Tel'abim (Mbappe Speedhack), we managed to kill ES HM weeks before BWL was released and we were less than 30 to do that, we also got first C'thun server kill as well as KT recently (both times the day after it was released).

I'm not the best at pressing keys or the one with the best reflexes, far from it, i start to get old  turtle_tongue_head   but one thing i'm good at is theorycrafting.

I played hunter back in the day from vanilla to Wotlk, then stopped for years, when i saw wow classic hardmode, nostalgia arrived, but after watching at people dying from server lags, i finally chosed to start on Tel'abim who was about to open.

The main reason i came on Twow was because i discovered you added steady shot as hunter skill and haste / armor penetration as new stats. I knew then after looking at your database than hunter would be very (very) good at dpsing unlike back in the day during vanilla where hunter was the worst dps.   hiding_smth_turtle_head

The reason for that is haste (from the stuff ofc but even more important from improved aspect proc : 5% chance per ranged attack to increase ranged attack speed by 30% for 12s), for other physical damage dealers, 1% haste only increase auto-attack damage, because auto attack is 50 to 60% of their total damage, it's a 0.5 to 0.6% damage increase. However for hunter it's nearly as good as for casters.

Because our rotation is basicaly : autoshot, steady shot, autoshot, steady shot, auto, steady, etc. (with one steady being replaced by a multishot once every 10s). So if we shot 10% faster, not only we will shot 10% more autoshot, but also 10% more steady shot.

Because autoshot + steadyshot represent 90% of our total damage against single target and 85%+ overall (the last 10% / 15% come from multishot who is not affected by haste), that means 1% haste = +0.85 to +0.9% damage and the proc from improved aspect was +25/27% damage for 12s (before the current big nerf) which was Huge.

Crit have some kind of diminishing returns as you can see here : ![Image](https://i.imgur.com/bzAG9N8.jpeg)
The more crit rate you have, the less gaining 1% crit increase your damage.

No diminishing returns for haste, let say your base ranged attack speed including quiver haste is 2.5 and you gain 1%, 1%, 1%, 2%, 2%, 2% and 3% haste from different sources. You could say it's 12% haste total so your new attack speed would be 2.5/1.12=2.232 but in game it's different, it's actually 2.5/1.01/1.01/1.01/1.02/1.02/1.02/1.03=2.219. the difference is thin but it's still better. In fact it means than no matter how much haste you got or haste effect or proc you are under,
gaining 1 extra % of haste will always be give the same damage increase (0.85 to 0.9%).

That means that once you're in full naxx gear, because of your very high crit rate, 1% haste will become as good as 1% crit.

I wanted to explain why haste is good because it will help when reviewing the new patch. I will talk first about PVE then later about pvp.

 **Beast Master spec**

The 2 bigs problems of BM were no scaling for the pet as well as a lack of Pet's survavibility. You adressed both, you did a pretty good job.
Few things to note however :
 -You nerfed pretty hard "swift aspects" : as i explained before haste is very good for hunter, this talent was (with mortal shots) the best in term of average ranged damage increase. You halved the damage bonus (from +26% damage to +13% under proc), but even if you doubled the proc chance to compensate, sure the uptime will increase but it will not be doubled, far from it. Giving +20% haste instead of +15 would be better, it would still be a nerf to the current version but not as big.
 -Intimidation : While it was indeed useless against mobs immune to stun, it's was still doing the job well 95 times out of 100, the job beeing for the Pet, to immediatly take back aggro.
With the new change, while it will be an improvement against mobs immune to stuns, against regular mobs, the pet will fail to take back aggro much more often than currently because a pet spend most of his time OOF (out of focus) and just use an ability every few second when he regenerate enough focus to use it before being OOF again.
The change I propose to resolve the problem is this one : reduce the threat buff duration from 8 to 4s but increase the threat by 100% instead of 50 and make Intimidation also restore 50 to 60 focus to the pet. This way when you'll use Intimidation, because the pet will also gain some focus, he will be able to do either growl + bite, or growl + claw, or lightning breath, or 2 claw or growl + screech, etc. This way it should be able to take back aggro most of the time.

Ferocity / Frenzy : it would be nice to reduce them to 3 pt talents because BM hunter still need to put 20 talent point outside of BM spec to be competitive in raid.

 **Survival new melee spec**

i was not a fan of a melee spec for hunter, not because it could not be good or fun to play, and to be honest, the way you did it will be good and fun to play, but because if you want to play a melee, there is already plenty of classes and specs to use with a large variety of gameplay, if you want to play a magical ranged damage dealer (caster), it's the same, but if you want to play a physical ranged damage healer (archer), there is only hunter and now, only 2 specs out of 3. The thing is, now the melee spec is here, it's not gonna change and we have to make the best of it.

First of all, it was pretty well implemented.
 -It emphasizes on slow 2H weapons, by having mongoose bite, wing clip and Carve all based on weapon damage, and it's a good thing as those weapons were underused. It will also make the spec much less vulnerable to Glancing Blows than it would be for dual wielding, because one auto attack out of two will be instead a raptor's Strike and will not be subject to Glancing for that reason (yellow hit).
 -Damaging traps were pretty bad, with the new scaling they will become pretty good.
 -Lightning reflexes make the current Hunter gear also very good for melee hunter.
 -Single Target damage from the melee weapon will be lower than ranged hunter but the fact mobs will be under fire trap effect / serpent sting nearly all the time, will make up for it and the total single target damage from melee hunter will be pretty close to a ranged one.
 -the real issue with this spec who will require big adjustments from the 2 other specs are the AOE potential.

 **About AOE potential :**

 -With lightning reflexes, a melee hunter will get significantly more MAP than an equally geared ranged hunter will get RAP, agility will increase both the same way, those 10% more agi will compensate the loss of trueshot aura. Both aspects of wolf and hawk gives the same increase of AP. But as a Melee Hunter you'll benefit from some strong Melee Attack Power buffs who don't apply to range such as Battle Shoot or Blessing of Might, and i don't talk about melee only consumables like wintefall firewater, strength pots, etc.
A naxx geared hunter have 2K+ RAP buffed, a new Naxx geared melee hunter will get 2K4+.

We know the damage scaling values :
Immolation Trap DoT: 1 extra tick damage for every 10 Attack Power
Explosive Trap Initial Damage: 1 extra damage for every 6.5 Attack Power
Explosive Trap DoT: 1 extra tick damage for every 30 Attack Power
and Trap mastery talent increase fire damage from traps by 30%

Explosive trap damage is 208 to 265 initial explosion (average 236.5) and then 330 over 20s, 33 per tick each 2s.
With Stinged Nettle Lacing new talent, explosive (and immolation) trap will also apply 2 tick of serpent sting.

with the scaling for our naxx geared hunter it will be :
Explosion : (236.5+(2400/6.5))*1.3=787
Dot Tick : (33+(2400/30))*1.3=147 every 2s
Serpent sting tick will deal (555/5)*1.3 = 144 every 3s

We can now see the total AOE damage per target during 6s (because volley last 6s and when we AOE mobs, they rarely live more than 8 to 10s anyway).
 787+(147*3)+(144*2) = 1516 damage per target (252 dps per target).

Those numbers by themselves are totally fine, a Naxx geared mage or warlock for example will have no problem dealing better AOE damage than a Melee hunter, but still, this spec change hunter from the worst AOE damage dealing class into a solid one with survival spec.

While it's not a problem because it will not make this spec OP versus other classes (it will not be OP but it will be pretty good). It will make it the best spec for Hunter in raid, specially for Speeds Runs where clearing trashs fast is very important, I do speed runs with my guild, I like it as many other guilds do, so i will use this melee spec because i don't want to penalise my teamates but it's where i have a problem with the hunter class change regarding PVE.

When the vast majority of people who created a Hunter did it to be a ranged physical damage dealer like i did myself and the clear best spec for PVE become a melee spec, it's a big concern.

 **Luckily there is solutions to this AOE issue :**

For MM spec :
Volley is by far the worst AOE spell in the game, 1 min cd, 80 damage per sec. for 6s, it's a channeling spell and with no scaling (technicaly there is some scaling on spell damage, but it's not a problem as if you increase SP on your stuff, you'll lose RAP at the same time). The problem with this spell is that for a Naxx geared hunter, if there is less than 8 target, it's actually a loss of dps over a standard ranged dps rotation. For Naxx, it's only decent for the packs of small spiders who patrol, few trashs groups before patchwerk and before Faerlina. and even there, it will only increase your damage by like 20% over standard damage rotation, and because of the long CD, only on 1 pack out of 2 or 3.

Solution : change base damage from 80 to 120 (this increase will also help a bit BM AOE potential without making volley good enough to be used by survival melee specs), reduce the base cooldown by 30s to reduce the problem i mentionned earlier about 1 pack out of 2 or 3, change Barrage talent from +15% volley damage to increase the periodic damage of volley by 3/6/9% of your ranged attack power.

For our naxx geared hunter with 2K RAP, it would be 120+(0.09*2000)=300 damage per tick (each second for 6 seconds).
You might say, hey 300 dps is better than the 252dps from explosive trap. But it's only a 48 dps increase for each target affected.
Don't forget Volley is a channeled spell so you'll do only that during those 6s, a melee hunter, one the other hand, will still do full melee damage (hundreds of dps from autoattack, raptor strike, mongoose bite, carve, wingclip) on top of those 252 dps of AOE damage from explosive trap, because traps are instant and only took one gcd. Keep in mind also than explosive trap deal even more damage because it continue to tick for up to 20s, not only 6s, for the MM hunter to beat a surv hunter on an AOE during those 6s, you'll need enough targets for those 48 more dps multiplicated by the number of targets to be higher than the full melee dps of the surv. hunter (hundreds of dps) which realisticaly can only happen when there will be 8 to 10+ targets while on most trashs mobs packs (2 to 7 mobs per pack), surv hunter will be much better.

For BM spec :

Increasing AOE damage from BM spec is not the easiest thing to do, the small increase from the volley base damage would help a bit but will be far from enough.
Sure you could lower again the cooldown of gorilla AOE but we don't want all raid pets to become gorillas.

my solution is :
Bestial Wrath : add to the current effect : when the pet is under bestial wrath, all his attacks will now also sweep any enemy who is close to his main target.
Just be aware than if a warrior who cleave can easily move 1 yard left or right to make sure his cleave hit the most enemies, a pet cannot be controled like that, so it might be good thing to increase pet melee range only during BW like you did with warriors using polearms. there will be no consequences on the pvp side as people will learn quickly to not stay near the main target of the pet to not be cleaved.

You can also reduce a bit the cooldown and duration (from 120 to 90s and last 15s instead of 18) as you nerfed the damage already.

 **MM spec**

Improved steady shot : pretty bad talent because it increase only bonus damage which doesn't scale, on top of that this bonus damage is only 50 so it's a 12.5 damage increase, it's bad.
Solution : Make it increase steady shot total damage by 3/6% or 4%/8%, at least it will scale with hunter gear and become significant.

Piercing shots : While the damage increase is good, it's a very bad design to upgrade hunter dps, it's another talent who will be ok with average hunters and penalise the good ones. When i pve, either on 5 man dungeons, 10 and 20 mans raid or 40 mans raid, i use scatter shot, or even FD/trap directly a lot in a broad range of situations because it's a reliable CC. And now because of this talent that you have to take because it's a significant dps upgrade and your main role as a hunter is to dps, your scattershot will often fail just because the mob will get a random bleed.
Solution : Of course you could change scatter to not break on bleeds, same for frost trap (frost stop the bleeding) but you can also change it for something else, with the name piercing shot, an easy change would be to make it give some armor penetration on your ranged attacks like serrated blade from rogue. You can also increase ranged haste by a few %, change the name in this case.
Also Hunter is already the class (with war) who scale the best with crits, it doesn't make sense to push even more on them, by making crits so much more powerful than normal hit and with the addition of Endless Quiver procs, when stars will align (crits and procs), we will kill naxx geared people in few globals then they will complain that hunter is OP.

Ranged weapon specialisation : it would be nice to turn it into a 3 pt talents.

 **PVP**

The way melee hunter works will make it really challenging to balance it for pvp, mainly because currently, it can do the same damage from range than a pre-patch survival was able to do. and it's the first time we have a spec who is at the same time very good at range and melee damage. And being able to trap every 15s while in combat is Huge, it might require some adjustements, fire traps in combat is fine, frost trap every 15s is already very powerful, but freezing every 15s might be too much.

However, while it can explain some nerfs like the fact they removed counterattack because it can really be abused as a melee hunter, the suppression of Counterattack hurt so bad the traditionnal ranged hunter, who now desesparately need a new tool to regain range.

Also the part of the talent "trap mastery" who reduce the chance for traps to be resisted need to return lower in survival tree for BM / MM to be able to pick it up. Losing Counterattack is already such a huge blow, we need trap to be reliable for all specs, a frost trap can be resisted when triggered but another check is made every 2s (or 1s if you're under DR on trap). so without the reduce trap resist talent, trap become unreliable.

But unlike for PVE where we have the numbers and can already know how things will go, for PVP, it's better to wait and test it. I will edit this post when we will be able to play and test those new specs.

 **Equipment :**

Haste is a very good stat for hunter, please add some haste on sets, on T2.5, you could remove spell power and add 1% haste on boots, spaulders and legs (who will finaly become better than those from exalted warsong)

On tier 3, it's the same, remove this useless mp5 (sure hunter is a mana class but the item point cost of mp5 is so expensive, it's not at all adapted for a class like hunter), you can, for example add, instead of mp5, 1% haste on ring, gloves and legs, because curently, there is 4 rings better than the T3 one, ES gloves are much better then T3 ones and there is 2 pairs of legs better than T3 ones, ES craft are bis (Dreamhide Leggings) then Leggings of Apocalypse.

Adding haste on T3.5 will also be great to stop with the crit inflation, our crit rates are already so high in naxx gear, adding armor pen can also work for that.

I hope my post will be helpful.
