Because our rotation is basicaly : autoshot, steady shot, autoshot, steady shot, auto, steady, etc. (with one steady being replaced by a multishot once every 10s). So if we shot 10% faster, not only we will shot 10% more autoshot, but also 10% more steady shot.

Because autoshot + steadyshot represent 90% of our total damage against single target and 85%+ overall (the last 10% / 15% come from multishot who is not affected by haste), that means 1% haste = +0.85 to +0.9% damage and the proc from improved aspect was +25/27% damage for 12s (before the current big nerf) which was Huge.

Crit have some kind of diminishing returns as you can see here :
The more crit rate you have, the less gaining 1% crit increase your damage.

No diminishing returns for haste, let say your base ranged attack speed including quiver haste is 2.5 and you gain 1%, 1%, 1%, 2%, 2%, 2% and 3% haste from different sources. You could say it's 12% haste total so your new attack speed would be 2.5/1.12=2.232 but in game it's different, it's actually 2.5/1.01/1.01/1.01/1.02/1.02/1.02/1.03=2.219. the difference is thin but it's still better. In fact it means than no matter how much haste you got or haste effect or proc you are under,
gaining 1 extra % of haste will always be give the same damage increase (0.85 to 0.9%).

That means that once you're in full naxx gear, because of your very high crit rate, 1% haste will become as good as 1% crit.

I wanted to explain why haste is good because it will help when reviewing the new patch. I will talk first about PVE then later about pvp.

Beast Master spec

The 2 bigs problems of BM were no scaling for the pet as well as a lack of Pet's survavibility. You adressed both, you did a pretty good job.
Few things to note however :
-You nerfed pretty hard "swift aspects" : as i explained before haste is very good for hunter, this talent was (with mortal shots) the best in term of average ranged damage increase. You halved the damage bonus (from +26% damage to +13% under proc), but even if you doubled the proc chance to compensate, sure the uptime will increase but it will not be doubled, far from it. Giving +20% haste instead of +15 would be better, it would still be a nerf to the current version but not as big.
-Intimidation : While it was indeed useless against mobs immune to stun, it's was still doing the job well 95 times out of 100, the job beeing for the Pet, to immediatly take back aggro.
With the new change, while it will be an improvement against mobs immune to stuns, against regular mobs, the pet will fail to take back aggro much more often than currently because a pet spend most of his time OOF (out of focus) and just use an ability every few second when he regenerate enough focus to use it before being OOF again.
The change I propose to resolve the problem is this one : reduce the threat buff duration from 8 to 4s but increase the threat by 100% instead of 50 and make Intimidation also restore 50 to 60 focus to the pet. This way when you'll use Intimidation, because the pet will also gain some focus, he will be able to do either growl + bite, or growl + claw, or lightning breath, or 2 claw or growl + screech, etc. This way it should be able to take back aggro most of the time.

Ferocity / Frenzy : it would be nice to reduce them to 3 pt talents because BM hunter still need to put 20 talent point outside of BM spec to be competitive in raid.

Survival new melee spec

i was not a fan of a melee spec for hunter, not because it could not be good or fun to play, and to be honest, the way you did it will be good and fun to play, but because if you want to play a melee, there is already plenty of classes and specs to use with a large variety of gameplay, if you want to play a magical ranged damage dealer (caster), it's the same, but if you want to play a physical ranged damage healer (archer), there is only hunter and now, only 2 specs out of 3. The thing is, now the melee spec is here, it's not gonna change and we have to make the best of it.

First of all, it was pretty well implemented.
-It emphasizes on slow 2H weapons, by having mongoose bite, wing clip and Carve all based on weapon damage, and it's a good thing as those weapons were underused. It will also make the spec much less vulnerable to Glancing Blows than it would be for dual wielding, because one auto attack out of two will be instead a raptor's Strike and will not be subject to Glancing for that reason (yellow hit).
-Damaging traps were pretty bad, with the new scaling they will become pretty good.
-Lightning reflexes make the current Hunter gear also very good for melee hunter.
-Single Target damage from the melee weapon will be lower than ranged hunter but the fact mobs will be under fire trap effect / serpent sting nearly all the time, will make up for it and the total single target damage from melee hunter will be pretty close to a ranged one.
-the real issue with this spec who will require big adjustments from the 2 other specs are the AOE potential.

About AOE potential :

-With lightning reflexes, a melee hunter will get significantly more MAP than an equally geared ranged hunter will get RAP, agility will increase both the same way, those 10% more agi will compensate the loss of trueshot aura. Both aspects of wolf and hawk gives the same increase of AP. But as a Melee Hunter you'll benefit from some strong Melee Attack Power buffs who don't apply to range such as Battle Shoot or Blessing of Might, and i don't talk about melee only consumables like wintefall firewater, strength pots, etc.
A naxx geared hunter have 2K+ RAP buffed, a new Naxx geared melee hunter will get 2K4+.

We know the damage scaling values :
Immolation Trap DoT: 1 extra tick damage for every 10 Attack Power
Explosive Trap Initial Damage: 1 extra damage for every 6.5 Attack Power
Explosive Trap DoT: 1 extra tick damage for every 30 Attack Power
and Trap mastery talent increase fire damage from traps by 30%

Explosive trap damage is 208 to 265 initial explosion (average 236.5) and then 330 over 20s, 33 per tick each 2s.
With Stinged Nettle Lacing new talent, explosive (and immolation) trap will also apply 2 tick of serpent sting.

with the scaling for our naxx geared hunter it will be :
Explosion : (236.5+(2400/6.5))*1.3=787
Dot Tick : (33+(2400/30))*1.3=147 every 2s
Serpent sting tick will deal (555/5)*1.3 = 144 every 3s

We can now see the total AOE damage per target during 6s (because volley last 6s and when we AOE mobs, they rarely live more than 8 to 10s anyway).
787+(147*3)+(144*2) = 1516 damage per target (252 dps per target).

Those numbers by themselves are totally fine, a Naxx geared mage or warlock for example will have no problem dealing better AOE damage than a Melee hunter, but still, this spec change hunter from the worst AOE damage dealing class into a solid one with survival spec.

While it's not a problem because it will not make this spec OP versus other classes (it will not be OP but it will be pretty good). It will make it the best spec for Hunter in raid, specially for Speeds Runs where clearing trashs fast is very important, I do speed runs with my guild, I like it as many other guilds do, so i will use this melee spec because i don't want to penalise my teamates but it's where i have a problem with the hunter class change regarding PVE.

When the vast majority of people who created a Hunter did it to be a ranged physical damage dealer like i did myself and the clear best spec for PVE become a melee spec, it's a big concern.

Luckily there is solutions to this AOE issue :

For MM spec :
Volley is by far the worst AOE spell in the game, 1 min cd, 80 damage per sec. for 6s, it's a channeling spell and with no scaling (technicaly there is some scaling on spell damage, but it's not a problem as if you increase SP on your stuff, you'll lose RAP at the same time). The problem with this spell is that for a Naxx geared hunter, if there is less than 8 target, it's actually a loss of dps over a standard ranged dps rotation. For Naxx, it's only decent for the packs of small spiders who patrol, few trashs groups before patchwerk and before Faerlina. and even there, it will only increase your damage by like 20% over standard damage rotation, and because of the long CD, only on 1 pack out of 2 or 3.

Solution : change base damage from 80 to 120 (this increase will also help a bit BM AOE potential without making volley good enough to be used by survival melee specs), reduce the base cooldown by 30s to reduce the problem i mentionned earlier about 1 pack out of 2 or 3, change Barrage talent from +15% volley damage to increase the periodic damage of volley by 3/6/9% of your ranged attack power.

For our naxx geared hunter with 2K RAP, it would be 120+(0.09*2000)=300 damage per tick (each second for 6 seconds).
You might say, hey 300 dps is better than the 252dps from explosive trap. But it's only a 48 dps increase for each target affected.
Don't forget Volley is a channeled spell so you'll do only that during those 6s, a melee hunter, one the other hand, will still do full melee damage (hundreds of dps from autoattack, raptor strike, mongoose bite, carve, wingclip) on top of those 252 dps of AOE damage from explosive trap, because traps are instant and only took one gcd. Keep in mind also than explosive trap deal even more damage because it continue to tick for up to 20s, not only 6s, for the MM hunter to beat a surv hunter on an AOE during those 6s, you'll need enough targets for those 48 more dps multiplicated by the number of targets to be higher than the full melee dps of the surv. hunter (hundreds of dps) which realisticaly can only happen when there will be 8 to 10+ targets while on most trashs mobs packs (2 to 7 mobs per pack), surv hunter will be much better.

For BM spec :

Increasing AOE damage from BM spec is not the easiest thing to do, the small increase from the volley base damage would help a bit but will be far from enough.
Sure you could lower again the cooldown of gorilla AOE but we don't want all raid pets to become gorillas.

my solution is :
Bestial Wrath : add to the current effect : when the pet is under bestial wrath, all his attacks will now also sweep any enemy who is close to his main target.
Just be aware than if a warrior who cleave can easily move 1 yard left or right to make sure his cleave hit the most enemies, a pet cannot be controled like that, so it might be good thing to increase pet melee range only during BW like you did with warriors using polearms. there will be no consequences on the pvp side as people will learn quickly to not stay near the main target of the pet to not be cleaved.

You can also reduce a bit the cooldown and duration (from 120 to 90s and last 15s instead of 18) as you nerfed the damage already.


MM spec

Improved steady shot : pretty bad talent because it increase only bonus damage which doesn't scale, on top of that this bonus damage is only 50 so it's a 12.5 damage increase, it's bad.
Solution : Make it increase steady shot total damage by 3/6% or 4%/8%, at least it will scale with hunter gear and become significant.

Piercing shots : While the damage increase is good, it's a very bad design to upgrade hunter dps, it's another talent who will be ok with average hunters and penalise the good ones. When i pve, either on 5 man dungeons, 10 and 20 mans raid or 40 mans raid, i use scatter shot, or even FD/trap directly a lot in a broad range of situations because it's a reliable CC. And now because of this talent that you have to take because it's a significant dps upgrade and your main role as a hunter is to dps, your scattershot will often fail just because the mob will get a random bleed.
Solution : Of course you could change scatter to not break on bleeds, same for frost trap (frost stop the bleeding) but you can also change it for something else, with the name piercing shot, an easy change would be to make it give some armor penetration on your ranged attacks like serrated blade from rogue. You can also increase ranged haste by a few %, change the name in this case.
Also Hunter is already the class (with war) who scale the best with crits, it doesn't make sense to push even more on them, by making crits so much more powerful than normal hit and with the addition of Endless Quiver procs, when stars will align (crits and procs), we will kill naxx geared people in few globals then they will complain that hunter is OP.

Ranged weapon specialisation : it would be nice to turn it into a 3 pt talents.


PVP

The way melee hunter works will make it really challenging to balance it for pvp, mainly because currently, it can do the same damage from range than a pre-patch survival was able to do. and it's the first time we have a spec who is at the same time very good at range and melee damage. And being able to trap every 15s while in combat is Huge, it might require some adjustements, fire traps in combat is fine, frost trap every 15s is already very powerful, but freezing every 15s might be too much.

However, while it can explain some nerfs like the fact they removed counterattack because it can really be abused as a melee hunter, the suppression of Counterattack hurt so bad the traditionnal ranged hunter, who now desesparately need a new tool to regain range.

Also the part of the talent "trap mastery" who reduce the chance for traps to be resisted need to return lower in survival tree for BM / MM to be able to pick it up. Losing Counterattack is already such a huge blow, we need trap to be reliable for all specs, a frost trap can be resisted when triggered but another check is made every 2s (or 1s if you're under DR on trap). so without the reduce trap resist talent, trap become unreliable.

But unlike for PVE where we have the numbers and can already know how things will go, for PVP, it's better to wait and test it. I will edit this post when we will be able to play and test those new specs.

Equipment :

Haste is a very good stat for hunter, please add some haste on sets, on T2.5, you could remove spell power and add 1% haste on boots, spaulders and legs (who will finaly become better than those from exalted warsong)

On tier 3, it's the same, remove this useless mp5 (sure hunter is a mana class but the item point cost of mp5 is so expensive, it's not at all adapted for a class like hunter), you can, for example add, instead of mp5, 1% haste on ring, gloves and legs, because curently, there is 4 rings better than the T3 one, ES gloves are much better then T3 ones and there is 2 pairs of legs better than T3 ones, ES craft are bis (Dreamhide Leggings) then Leggings of Apocalypse.

Adding haste on T3.5 will also be great to stop with the crit inflation, our crit rates are already so high in naxx gear, adding armor pen can also work for that.

I hope my post will be helpful.

Then i'm gonna talk about MM spec, things will be different for BM and Surv because AP increase Pet and trap damage respectively and will be significantly better for those 2 specs, unfortunately i cannot test it, i don't have a good 2H weapon for Surv. and scorpid (who should be the best performing pet on bosses, when he have enough time to stack poison) is currently bugged for BM (scorpid poison doesn't scale with Spirit Bond talent : <https://turtlecraft.gg/bug-report?id=9369>)

Then if you want to compare agi / haste / crit / AP / hit, it depend on your hunter and his gear :

 1% hit is always a (slightly more than) 1% damage increase until you reach hit cap.
 1% haste is around 0.9% damage increase on bosses (single target) and 0.85% damage increase overall.
 1% crit, for that, look the chart in my first post, but for a naxx geared hunter, it would be around 0.9% when raid buffed.
agility can be decomposed in crit and AP. (53 agi increase crit chance by 1%, 1 agi = 2 RAP)

The big question is how much AP you need to increase your damage by 1%, to be able to compare AP / agi with the other stats.

For that the easiest way, once fully buffed and equipped for raid with your passive trinkets, is to :
 1. open your character panel in game and mouseover ranged damage to check the DPS (309 in my case).
 2. unequip and equip back an attack power item and check the DPS difference, to know how much AP you need to increase your dps by 1 (10 in my case, it's 14 without any haste, but quiver and haste on your equipment, buffs will reduce it).
 3. add regular permanent AP buffs who are not taken into account in the character panel, for example, 110 attack power from hunter mark, 200 AP against undead from the 2 consecrated sharpened stones, etc. (for me, as i don't have KT trinket for another 150 AP against undead, it's 310 AP to add which worth 31 dps)

Then you can compare, in my case my total DPS is 309+31 = 340 DPS. 1% of that would be 3.4 dps, and i need 34 attack power to increase my DPS by 3.4 which is 1% extra damage.

I can easily make the comparaison now.

author: therealrexxar
subject: Please try to compromise with players
content_md:
Hello again fellow hunters,

I have come to terms with devs making these big changes in the next patch. However, I still think that they should strongly consider the feedback given by players here in the forums and on discord, particularly when it comes to changes that affected the old way of playing the classes and specs.

 *"Our philosophy has always been focusing on enhancing and polishing the existing identity of classes and specializations, rather than reworking or replacing them entirely. As fun as some more wacky concepts may be, we want to keep true to the identity of vanilla classes. This means smaller and less drastic changes overall, which should culminate in a healthy meta allowing each class and specialization to shine in their own way."*

This feels like it hasn't been the case right now with the new patch coming in a few days. I think that they should at least try to reach a compromise with players that liked things the way they were before. That would make a strong case on why Turtle WoW is different from the rest of the private servers out there on how devs communicate with and respect the playerbase.

Some of the changes I have heard before (and which I agree with the most) that players have not been very happy about include:
 1. Changes to Viper Sting
 2. Removing Counterattack
 3. Changes to Wing Clip (this should no longer an issue since the CD will be reduced to 3sec)
 4. Changes to Mongoose Bite
 5. Big overhaul on Surv tree and how strongly tied it is to "Melee Hunter" (what about BM?)
 6. Removing Wyvern Sting
 7. New scaling talents for Surv and BM trees are not very "vanilla" (related to point 5)

I hope in the future that these changes will be reconsidered (not necessarily reverted, of course, but perhaps adjusted) to try to make all players happy.

Thanks for coming to my TED talk.

author: Ragetto
subject: Re: Please try to compromise with players
content_md:
> **Xudo wrote: Tue Oct 29, 2024 10:01 am**
> What kind of skill you need to counter Wingclip spam?

What kind of hunter would "spam" Wing Clip except to save their life and get out of the dead zone?

If a hunter is spamming Wing Clip, it’s because they keep getting parried or dodged, probably while taking hits in close combat. Hunters don't want to be in a situation where they have to spam Wing Clip!

Of course, occasionally they might spam it across multiple targets (in very specific cases - like helping a flag carrier escape in WSG with no useful cooldowns up), but most hunters won’t do this.

> **Xudo wrote: Tue Oct 29, 2024 10:01 am**
> What kind of skill you need to counter Viper Sting spam?

Multiple classes can dispel it, and when they do, the hunter ends up wasting more mana than they drained - especially since hunters don’t have much to begin with. If they’re just spamming, they’ll be out of mana faster than their target, so in a way, the cooldown prevents clueless hunters from ooming themselves...

I can say this as a PvP healing priest who faces a lot of hunters in BGs. Viper Sting is annoying, sure, but there’s always a way to mitigate its impact.

Basic mana management, using potions/teas only at the end of the drain (rather than mid-drain if you’re about to be oom), keeping good positioning (LOS + make sure teammates are between you and the hunters), and asking for dispels or killing pets so you can regen a few ticks (ideally as often as possible during fights). Don’t want to get drained by hunters? Stay alert and always keep an eye on them, where they are, where they’re going, and if they’re targeting you.

These are many little differences between mediocre and good players. But with no actual PvP experience (like high-level arenas pre-Twow), it’s easy to overlook 80% of these details.

author: Zvyrhol
subject: Re: Please try to compromise with players
content_md:
I highly doubt changes made to Hunter were made by experienced PvP Hunters. In my opinion Hunter received the worst changes to PvP from all classes.

I don't know this class well but I have faced them a lot in battlegrounds - Hunter is the enemy I know. I know Hunter's weak and strong points. They are very efficient with draining mana and keeping enemy at bay with Wing Clip, sometimes they even shine with slowing everyone, traps are good too if in good hands, same for Wyvern Sting.

If you think about it, all strong points about Hunter are about their extremely effective annoyance in PvP. My impression after the changes is that PvP CC2 council hated Hunters for their annoyance so they decided to nerf every annoying part of their toolkit.

Viper Sting seems to be useless now, at least in group fights where it used to be effective.
Wing Clip with 3 seconds CD makes Hunter vulnerable in close fights - this is game changing because it has never been a problem, all Hunters already know they will have hard time defending against Rogues/Warriors or other melees.
Talents spent on traps are changed a bit I think (correct me if I'm wrong).
Wyvern Sting is completely gone, I know it wasn't used a lot but some people used it in PvP.

I don't play Hunter but these nerfs seem to be massive in PvP for me, Priest the observer.
I observe that devs and CC2 council decided to transfer Hunter's PvP strong points from useful (and annoying) toolkit to pure brainless DPS which is bad, I think all PvPers can agree here.

Why was Hunter hurt so much? It's not clear who made mistake. Devs, CC2 council non-Hunters. Or maybe there were indeed 0 PvP Hunters in the council.

author: Steakhouse
subject: Re: Leveling talents
content_md:
Definitely BM. Imp revive and Intimidation are incredible in particular.

With the 8 first defensive talents you nearly double your pet's survivability. It's safer in HC, and also faster in terms of xp/hour.

Imp revive means you can res your pet in combat with as little as a conc shot if you're far away, or with scare beast / freeze trap for good measure. It also generally means you can take a lot more risks for the sake of efficiency.

I haven't tried the new Intimidation, the old one functioned as a pseudo taunt while leveling ; I reckon this one will scale better at high level. At any rate threat on your pet means it can hold two mobs that you can AoE with multi shot/carve, boom trap, and spreading serpent stings. Send pet with intimidation on a baddie, and after one growl, send it to another. The first mob will likely die before it can melee you. I reckon this will be particularly strong with Screech.

In general 1.17.2 added scaling in BM but one thing remains the same: your pet's base stats are very high, especially when leveling, and BM makes them better.

author: Bob022
subject: Re: Bm leveling talents
content_md:
Bestial Swiftness is now a combination talent, and a no-brainer at 1 point.  You get 3% pet haste, pet movement speed, and improved aspects.  That's great value for one point.

Bestial Discipline is traditionally considered weak for what it does, seldom recommended outside a few niche strategies (if you're doing these, you don't need to ask about it).  A leveling character will usually get better quality of life out of a point in Mend Pet for the cure effect.  That being said, neither is going to make or break a build.

Note that Growl is traditionally not an actual taunt, but rather an ability that adds a flat amount of additional threat.  As such it tends to work better on autocast rather than trying to save it like a taunt.  This assumes Growl wasn't turned into a genuine taunt with 1.17.2 without my noticing, although I've heard no such claims.

Freeing up points:  Elusiveness is optional and should be thought of as discretionary.  If you need to free up an extra point someplace, you can usually drop a point out of Frenzy (to 4/5) and it's alright.  That last point has somewhat diminished returns, especially for people using pets with high attack speeds.  For solo PvE, you don't necessarily need 5/5 Endurance Training.  Pet health regenerates very rapidly between pulls and Mend Pet will heal the same amount whether your pet has 4000 HP or 3500.  That can free up a couple points.  Even if these talents are added later, freeing up these points early on can allow the player to obtain other, more critical talents sooner.

For the most part, the talents are pretty self-explanatory and the big choice for a leveling Beast Mastery hunter will amount to when he wants to go 11 into Marksman for Steady Shot--you'll get it, just a question of when, and particularly when you want it versus Intimidation or Bestial Wrath.

author: Neechy
subject: Remove Hunter Carve Ability
content_md:
Why is no one talking about the abomination that is the new Carve ability?

Is it fun to use? Sure.
Is it authentic to hunter class fantasy? Absolutely not.
Why is a hunter (the only RANGED physical class) hitting more targets with one move than say a warrior, the quintessential close combat juggernaut tank class.

Does someone have a sound argument to justify why Carve was added and why it should stay in the game? It was silly when added in SoD and it is silly here. (And please don't say "because Rexxar had Carve!!" - you can't design a whole class over one outlier who is a hero character in a RTS game...)

I have reviewed pretty much all the player sentiments on class changes so far. While I agree with some players who would have preferred bare minimum class changes, I can also agree with TWoW's decision to make melee hunters more viable. I think it's not a bad idea for Survival to be melee focused (though ideally should still preserve some range functionality so as to clearly differentiate it from other melee classes like warriors).

That said, you can have a strong and fun-to-play melee hunter without completely jumping the shark by adding an ability like Carve. The ridiculous thing about Carve is not just the amount of targets it hits and the short CD, but also that it is only 3 rows deep in the Survival tree, meaning literally all hunter specs, including BM or MM can now dip into Survival to become ridiculous AoE machines.

From a class in Vanilla wow and even all throughout Wotlk+ that was loved for its unique physical ranged class identity using its pets and traps to stay a distance to now just becoming some AoE tank abomination, this change just feels like a massive overstep.

What even is the logistics being Carve supposed to be? We are supposed to be believe some ranged hunter who also happens to be skilled in close combat just whips out his big weapon and with a "sweeping attack" hits 5 targets, which is more than any other class can hit with a weapon strike? Why are big bad warriors hitting less targets with their cleaves? The fantasy behind this just makes no sense.

My suggestion?
If melee hunter is here to stay, then give it a cleave ability that is MUCH DEEPER in the Survival tree, to demonstrate that its mastery of melee combat has allowed it to now hit multiple targets at once. But DON'T make it 5, that is just ridiculous. Just make it a regular cleave in the vein of hunters and rogues. Survival tree shouldn't be AoE, it should just be standard melee with a heavy focus on trap utility to make it interesting and unique.

Apologies for the rant, but as we all know this update was pretty extreme, and seeing abilities like Carve added just worry me about the direction the server is going.

I applaud the developers for their hard work and their passion, I just hope that they can make flavour changes without vastly overhauling class identities. Interested to hear others thoughts on this as well. Cheers.   hiding_smth_turtle_head

I have reviewed pretty much all the player sentiments on class changes so far. While I agree with some players who would have preferred bare minimum class changes, I can also agree with TWoW's decision to make melee hunters more viable. I think it's not a bad idea for Survival to be melee focused (though ideally should still preserve some range functionality so as to clearly differentiate it from other melee classes like warriors).

That said, you can have a strong and fun-to-play melee hunter without completely jumping the shark by adding an ability like Carve. The ridiculous thing about Carve is not just the amount of targets it hits and the short CD, but also that it is only 3 rows deep in the Survival tree, meaning literally all hunter specs, including BM or MM can now dip into Survival to become ridiculous AoE machines.

From a class in Vanilla wow and even all throughout Wotlk+ that was loved for its unique physical ranged class identity using its pets and traps to stay a distance to now just becoming some AoE tank abomination, this change just feels like a massive overstep.

What even is the logistics being Carve supposed to be? We are supposed to be believe some ranged hunter who also happens to be skilled in close combat just whips out his big weapon and with a "sweeping attack" hits 5 targets, which is more than any other class can hit with a weapon strike? Why are big bad warriors hitting less targets with their cleaves? The fantasy behind this just makes no sense.

My suggestion?
If melee hunter is here to stay, then give it a cleave ability that is MUCH DEEPER in the Survival tree, to demonstrate that its mastery of melee combat has allowed it to now hit multiple targets at once. But DON'T make it 5, that is just ridiculous. Just make it a regular cleave in the vein of hunters and rogues. Survival tree shouldn't be AoE, it should just be standard melee with a heavy focus on trap utility to make it interesting and unique.

Apologies for the rant, but as we all know this update was pretty extreme, and seeing abilities like Carve added just worry me about the direction the server is going.

I applaud the developers for their hard work and their passion, I just hope that they can make flavour changes without vastly overhauling class identities. Interested to hear others thoughts on this as well. Cheers.

I have to disagree, sharing a role and cooldown in this context effectively causes one of those abilities to be replaced by the other, you aren't going to be choosing between one or the other when one's often going to be preferred in most contexts.

> In my point of view, Carve = Multishot. Will it be better if all hunters had to melee-weave their multishot? I think no. Survival hunter identity IS being melee. So he should use melee weapon.

I think this is wrong. It *would* be better for them to have to weave Multi-Shot because melee-weaving is Survival's intended identity. They were always supposed to be spending half their time in melee and half their time at ranged, hence the access to poisons and the use of Improved Wingclip and (formerly) Counterattack. Their identity isn't just melee, it's the emphasis on the melee portion of the melee/ranged hybrid that is Hunter. I've said elsewhere before that while I don't think a pure-melee build shouldn't be an option, I do think it shouldn't be the primary path for the spec. Carve replacing Mutli-Shot in practice is just too transformative to the playstyle and identity of the spec.

> If you give shamans "fire totem of Meteorite", which deal high AoE physical damage and share cooldown with Fire Nova, it will be effectively the same spell.
>  If you give paladins "powerful fart", which deal periodic poison damage in 10 yd range, it will be effectively same spell as Concecration.

Those aren't very good examples because 1: those alternative spells would alter the flavor of the class, and 2: Carve and Multi-Shot aren't similar enough to be considered functionally identical like your examples describe. Multi-Shot is a targeted ability that hits 3 enemies, while Carve doesn't require a target and hits up to 5 in a cone. That's different enough for one to be used over the other for large packs, hence Neechy's point about the AoE-ification of gameplay, especially since it's high enough in the tree for other specs to have access to it. I don't think Carve would be as offensive if it was deeper in the tree and only hit 1 target and 2 adjacent mobs like Multi-Shot does.

> I don't propose to add anything to rogues. Their only "AoE" is blade flurry locked in Combat tree. It should stay as is.

This I can totally agree with.

content_md:
> **Xudo wrote: Wed Jan 22, 2025 1:00 pm**
> If you somehow remove deadzone of ranged abilities, then surv-hunter will still be ranged hunter.

I really don’t think that’d be the case since you’d need to build into the rest of the tree to make it that far, you’re not going to want to waste the points you already spent on improving your melee abilities. The goal is that it would be too deep in the tree for other specs to take and deep enough for the Survival Hunter to already be committed to using some up-close attacks. If the total removal of the deadzone somehow proves to be problematic despite having precedent for being baseline in TBC (as opposed to deep down in one tree here), then maybe it can simply reduce its range? Would a 1-yard deadzone be so bad? How about 2-yard? Limits like these don’t need to be set in stone as far as brainstormed ideas go.

> Melee-weaving is fun, but is is not "identity". It is minmaxing shit like totem/seal twisting. Might be fun to grasp, but require perfect internet connection to perform well.

The “identity” in this is the distinction between the fantasy of Aragorn/Strider over Legolas. Using both melee and ranged fits the guerilla-fighting, “use everything you have” fantasy. Melee-weaving is very much not a minmax engine-quirk like Twisting is, Vanilla’s lead class designer has said as much. He’s gone on to talk about Seal/Totem-Twisting and how it’s not an intended or ideal play pattern, and he’s specifically talked about how Survival was meant to be played with a 50/50 playstyle that alternates between ranged and melee evenly. If people say the spec lacked mechanical identity or a unique playstyle, then Weaving is right there as something to be leaned into. Optimal Melee-Weaving would definitely raise the ceiling in some aspects, but I think the basic gameplay of alternating shots and strikes has a pretty low skill-floor as far as playstyles go.

I don’t think you need a good internet connection to alternate an Arcane Shot with a Raptor Strike, or to autoattack and run out for a quick Serpent Sting. It’s not like you need a swing timer to see that your character’s finished their attack and can run back in/out for another. I know this because I have experience playing with poor internet connections, it doesn’t require the precise timing that Seal-Twisting does where you need a swing timer to see the exact moment before your auto-attack lands.
> The point of Carve was to add melee attack to melee-related tree.

I think the problem is that it pushes the spec too far into that direction. Again I don’t think a melee-only build should be impossible, it just shouldn’t be the main route for the spec.

> Making Carve to work like Cleave (on next melee attack) is acceptable incovenience too. It is better than cast time, because it is more natural to melees and allows you to move. But it still have to share CD with Multishot.

I’m honestly not 100% sure if a version of Carve like that should still share a cooldown with Multi-Shot, I can see a case for both outcomes, but I’m glad you also think mobility is an important aspect of the spec. The mobility aspect brings me back to Melee-Weaving as an encouraged (but not forced) playstyle, Survival’s supposed to have a mobile playstyle that alternates between ranged and melee, and I think “on next swing” abilities like Cleave would do well to encourage people to not just stay in one or the other when it comes to range vs. melee. I agree that Survival shouldn’t be pushed to spend all its time in ranged, but I don’t think it should be pushed to being only melee either.

I don’t think you need a good internet connection to alternate an Arcane Shot with a Raptor Strike, or to autoattack and run out for a quick Serpent Sting. It’s not like you need a swing timer to see that your character’s finished their attack and can run back in/out for another. I know this because I have experience playing with poor internet connections, it doesn’t require the precise timing that Seal-Twisting does where you need a swing timer to see the exact moment before your auto-attack lands.
The point of Carve was to add melee attack to melee-related tree.
I think the problem is that it pushes the spec too far into that direction. Again I don’t think a melee-only build should be impossible, it just shouldn’t be the main route for the spec.
Making Carve to work like Cleave (on next melee attack) is acceptable incovenience too. It is better than cast time, because it is more natural to melees and allows you to move. But it still have to share CD with Multishot.
I’m honestly not 100% sure if a version of Carve like that should still share a cooldown with Multi-Shot, I can see a case for both outcomes, but I’m glad you also think mobility is an important aspect of the spec. The mobility aspect brings me back to Melee-Weaving as an encouraged (but not forced) playstyle, Survival’s supposed to have a mobile playstyle that alternates between ranged and melee, and I think “on next swing” abilities like Cleave would do well to encourage people to not just stay in one or the other when it comes to range vs. melee. I agree that Survival shouldn’t be pushed to spend all its time in ranged, but I don’t think it should be pushed to being only melee either.

author: Ragetto
subject: Freezing Trap Effect Cancelled by PvP Trinket: Please "fix" it
content_md:
Hello!

 ------------------------------------------------------
 ------------------------------------------------------
 *Edit: Looking back, I’m fully in favor of reverting to the pre-CC2 trinket (which I believe was a design mistake). Blind, sap, and Freezing Trap shouldn’t be treated like spammable CCs such as sheep or fear.*
 ------------------------------------------------------
 ------------------------------------------------------

The Scatter-Trap combo was nerfed shortly before CC2, which was already a tough hit. Then CC2 arrived, destroying the classic PvP hunter build from Vanilla and replacing it with a melee tree (wtf) that no one uses in PvP.

But this change feels like the final nail in the coffin: the new PvP trinket cancels all control effects, including Freezing Trap.

Here’s why this is a massive issue (for hunters, at least...):

- 1) FD + Freezing Trap was often a last resort to avoid getting destroyed in melee.

- 2) Freezing Trap is far harder to land than a fear or sheep in most situations (if you want to trap a healer, you have to do something counterintuitive for a ranged DPS - especially for hunters, who have a dead zone: get close to them).

- 3) It’s not spammable > 15-sec cooldown (or effectively 30 seconds since it can’t be used in combat and requires Feign Death).
For these reasons, this control ability must be EXTREMELY reliable and predictable (especially since it can resist…) or it loses all its value.

Before CC2, traps could be dispelled, but it was predictable. If you saw a priest or paladin on the enemy team, you knew your trap could be easily countered. So you had to adapt your tactics and avoid wasting a 30-sec cooldown. Now, with this new trinket, there’s no way to plan ahead. It’s just like RNG *(unless you have cyborg eyes and a computer in your brain… and even then...)*

This completely goes against the PvP hunter’s identity built around control and anticipation.

So, my request is...
 **Please remove Freezing Trap from the list of control effects canceled by the PvP trinket.**
(or just revert the trinket to how it was before CC2)

Thank you for considering this!

subject: BM is now viable... forcing me to change race to Orc
content_md:
I always loved the idea of gnome and undead hunters, lore wise. In fact I was the first person to suggest these races as hunters years ago in the discord suggestions, based on lore and in game characters that are hunters of those races.

So when they added these races I started playing Twow as it was my ideal race-class combination purely for roleplay and  aesthetics.

Now... Beastmastery has got some love and it's now viable in raids, I always loved to make full use of my pets in raid, but had I known they would be this viable I would have chosen Orc for the pet damage racial...

Is it possible that we add epic questlines to learn a minor racial from other race?

Command from Orc.
Regeneration from Troll.
+5% Health from Tauren.

Human Spirit from Human

+%5 Intellect from Gnomes

These minor racials can have a significant effect on gameplay and are a gatekeeper for some people wanting to play other race than the "viable" one.

subject: Re: BM is now viable... forcing me to change race to Orc
content_md:
Orcs command is a 5% petdamage increase. If you are actively playing alongsidd your pet, thats a ~1-2% damage increase overall.

Its a conditional racial that only applies to certain fights (aka your guild night not want you to use hunter pets on fights where the pet can cause problems (zeliek, grobbulus, vael, twin emps come to mind). So Ou cant exactly balance it against other racials because of its conditionality.

Because if you balance racials between orc and dwarf hunter, the same racials will inevitably not be equal for a rogue of those two races.

So why boher when the nunber is so insignificant to begin with? It just detracts from the non mechanical aspects of the game and transforms the racials into some rude goldberg version of everyone does exactly more 1% damage. Its a lot of effort for something that does not matter in the slightest.

I always loved the idea of gnome and undead hunters, lore wise. In fact I was the first person to suggest these races as hunters years ago in the discord suggestions, based on lore and in game characters that are hunters of those races.

So when they added these races I started playing Twow as it was my ideal race-class combination purely for roleplay and aesthetics.

Now... Beastmastery has got some love and it's now viable in raids, I always loved to make full use of my pets in raid, but had I known they would be this viable I would have chosen Orc for the pet damage racial...

No I feel compelled to do a race swap to Orc since I am stacking all the pet bonuses for the hunter class...

Is it possible that we add epic questlines to learn a minor racial from other race?
Like, you can swap

Cannibalize from Undead.
Command from Orc.
Regeneration from Troll.
+5% Health from Tauren.

and for Alliance:
Human Spirit from Human
Dodge from Night Elves
Treasure Finding from Dwarves
+%5 Intellect from Gnomes

These minor racials can have a significant effect on gameplay and are a gatekeeper for some people wanting to play other race than the "viable" one.

I see turtle took a right step in this direction with the Ancient Warfare Text quests. I hope we can do something similar for these minor racials.
Nobody will give 2 fucks if you do 5% less dps

author: Jan125
subject: Re: hunter pet questions
content_md:
Note: With CC2, foxes now belong to their own family.
They can learn Grace (Dodge buff on themselves). I haven't checked Dash.

Lupos is a regular wolf.

In terms of raw damage, Wind Serpent (Lightning Breath spam), Serpent (Highest damage mod, no spammable ability), and Cat (Spammable and high damage mod) still reign.
For tanking, Owl, Bat, or Carrion Bird with Screech, due to AoE threat.

Sometimes, your pet may die, even though we now have AoE damage reduction with Avoidance.
Keep in mind that Furious Howl only affects melee hits.

author: ajax_808
subject: Re: hunter preraid bis gearing
content_md:
take a look at this:

[embed: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1BIlB2P1kyV_QdD4ULQzvZvS6hK6BDouUQkyHQzCvBGI/preview#gid=333718892]

I'ts a pretty cool tool that ive been using while I try to make my own turtle wow specific hunter pre-raid BiS list. Im starting with the standard vanilla items but also stuff from Hateforge Quarry, Stormwind Vault, karazhan Crypt, Black Morass, turtle wow specific quests, silvermoon remnant reputation rewards etc. Chance to hit requirement is also different with the weapon skill book and changes to hit chance calculations on Turtle. I'm currently using 7% Chance to hit as the required minimum and not considering chance to hit beyond that. There is a lot of variability surrounding the conversion between agility, crit chance and attack power that depends upon gear level, current spec and buffs but to compare by "AP equivalent" I've sort of landed on:

 1 Agi = 3 APeq
 1 crit chance = 30 APeq
 1 AP = 1 APeq

This only really works for PVE and marksmanship builds as it doesn't make any considerations for stamina, strength or armor as would be necessary for evaluating items for PvP or for a Survival builds. Ive been working on it for a week or so but it just takes a while to build out.

I'll post up the google sheet when I'm finished.  It will probably be ridiculed by the community for being flawed or incomplete but that is probably the best way to tweak it and make it more accurate.

I'll send a PM but the long and short of it is this; until the exact impact that haste/increased attack speed has on DPS can be predicted and replicated, I cant give an answer with complete certainty. That being said, trying to figure out the definitive pre-raid BIS list is still a fun academic exercise. I love that the items, talents and weapon skill calculations are all different enough from vanilla that we can't just copy paste a list from 20 years ago and have to figure it out. The testing I have done with attack speed has not given the expected results, so I'm still not sure where an item like the [Cloverlink Belt](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=61758) really falls in the pecking order. Additionally, there is the issue of what parameters to include and what is the endpoint. As for parameters, i was just talking with my brother about this, should reputation rewards be included? Should PvP items? If so do you put an arbitrary cap on PvP rank like rank 8 or rank 10? Some of that boils down to principle vs practicality, what is mathematically perfect vs what is reasonable.

author: Angelafarehart
subject: Re: It's time to pay attention to the hunters.
content_md:
It's safe to confirm atm hunters are complete bottom F tier in Turtle pvp. Spell push back on ranged attacks.. cant even beat casters like we always did because of this. a mage can just missile barrage and lock us down from fighting back, Aimed shot is completely worthless as theres virtually no time or window to ever pull it off due to its 3 second cast (which also has pushback)

we have deterance as talent in our survival tree because.... Why? (counterattack was removed so yeah)
we have no armor penetration from our steady shot or aimed shot to speak of. and our deadzone is a problem as it always has but somehow manages to be even worse here, when u consider how fast casters can burst you down, also for some reason you get dazed by shaman's lighting shield if u have cheetah on making them impossible to kite.

And to the ones posting here trying to disparage the fact hunters are clearly gimped, i already proved at least 1 person who actually has a hunter as a geared alt and went to pvp for a bit to see how bad they are now and successfully realised "oh wow you are right, this is just awful, sorry for doubting you."

So i urge you to see for yourself. Hunters are in desperate need of fixing and tuning upward.

author: Silhouette
subject: Re: It's time to pay attention to the hunters.
content_md:
It is sad that people come in, don't even take time to read the first sentence from OP and throw at us this irrelevant PvE sheet. Nevertheless, I doubt Twow is going to do anything with Class design in PvP anytime soon, since PvE is the main focus of the server and hunters are doing well in the PvE tierlist, devs will more than likely not question the class efficiency even if it's a whole different result in PvP.

Regarding Marksmanship in PvP: It is indeed pretty bad. Most classes have an incredible burst now, more anti-CC for everyone and more instantaneousness than Hunters do, most hunter abilities take time from the moment an arrow is fired to the moment it damages a target. Now PvP is about smashing your big CDs first, and depending on the class you play, you might win by design, CC2 amplifies that and everything will get incredibly worse with T3.5 adding way too much powerups to everyone.

In PvP, everything basically feel less skill-based and more and more gear-based where winning often relies on drawing your gun first, in a situation where vertical progression and careless PvP design don't mix at all for a better future.

author: Wolf of Rage
subject: Re: It's time to pay attention to the hunters.
content_md:
Based on how CC2 is looking so far, I would dread CC3.

Inbefore Rogues don't have any CC, ever, at all. Warriors only have one Ability: Execute. Blink is changed so that whenever a Mage uses it, they're sent to the shadow realm underneath all textures. Fear by Warlocks is now an unlimited AoE. Druids get Flight Form but since there's no flight here it just results in acting as another Ground Mount. Hunters' Auto Shot causes them to instead throw their Ranged Weapon at the enemy. Shamans' Windfury is renamed to "Windfurry". Shockadins are back but instead it's through the Holy Shock Aura from Diablo II and they deal 1-1M Damage completely at random. Priests' Mind Control allows them to unequip or delete the victim's worn gear. Thunderfury procs naked ladies.

On-topic, absurd Damage is normal. Watched some Classic videos of a lower-Level Dwarf Warrior with Engineering smoke max-Level/high-geared people sometimes within the timespan of a Global Cooldown (Slam/Death Ray + random Ability + Attack + Sapper, etc.) following a Crowd Control application. Then a video about a... naked Gnome Mage... doing the same.

Not sure how absurd Hunters can get here post-CC2 and with gear changes, as I've not had enough wild encounters with them myself - - the ones I've met I guess underperformed or preferred to go for the long fights. But generally if they have good WDMG + AP and you have low or currently reduced Armor, you should feel in danger.

subject: The Silent Trap
content_md: Hunter traps are affected by silence, meaning that you cannot put down a trap while silenced. This doesn't make sense as putting down a trap wouldn't have a verbal component to it like a spell. In fact you would want to place your trap as silently and stealthily as possible. This oversight negatively affects Survival Hunters as they can place traps in combat and it's a good portion of their DPS. Therefore please make it so that Hunters can put down their traps while silenced. Thank you and have a merry Christmas.

author: Raypulsif
subject: Hunter rotation (vanilla veteran but new to turtle)
content_md:
Hello there,
I come from official classic and played before on Kronos.
I only played vanilla wow, i never went tbc/etc
On vanilla and classic, my rotation was pretty much AS (Aimed shot), MS (multi shot), AA (auto shot) full cycle or clipped cycle, depending of the weapon attack speed, and an added Serpent Sting on start (no debuff slot limit on HC realms)

Now I joined Turtle early december, and I discover a new tree and new talents. It also seems somes changes happened recently.

I asked a guildie and he said you just spam SS (steady shot) "like TBC", which seems so weird to me.

I went a bit into research, found a small youtube video that said :
 - when weapon speed < 3.3 : AA MS AA SS AA SS
 - when weapon speed > 3.3 : AA SS MS AA SS [Serpent sting/arcane shot/aimed shot]
but the video is a bit old also (10 months), I don't know if it's still relevant, because perhaps there were a talent revamp after the release of the video

Not including Aimed shot or just discarding it feels weird.

What is the current "meta" and correct rotation for a MM spec ?
I have some ideas, but I could be completely wrong too

Thx for reading this message

author: Soulforged
subject: BB
content_md:
I will put this as simply as i can and will not tire you with technicals but keep it generic.

The recent insignia changes have drastically impacted my experience as a Hunter in PvP. These changes introduced a mechanic borrowed from a later expansion that allows players to break out of crowd control more frequently. While this may sound like a quality-of-life improvement, it fundamentally alters the dynamics of Vanilla PvP in ways that undermine class roles and balance.

I understand that your first thought might be that this is an overreaction but in my opinion this affects and impacts the hunter class more than any other class.

In Vanilla PvP, crowd control was a key aspect of strategy, with each class leveraging its unique toolkit to contribute to a team’s success. Hunters, in particular, relied on their ability to kite, control enemies with traps, and deal sustained damage from range. The original insignia design had a cooldown that required strategic use, creating windows of opportunity where Hunters could capitalize on their strengths. However, with the new insignia changes, crowd control effects are frequently negated, drastically reducing the effectiveness of Hunter traps and kiting strategies. This not only diminishes the Hunter’s role as a disruptor and ranged threat in group PvP but also makes the class feel less impactful overall.

In a PvP group setting, Hunters often filled a versatile role, providing utility and damage while controlling the battlefield with traps and zoning tools. With crowd control so easily countered, Hunters are now pushed toward a more generic damage-dealing role, which not only feels uninspired but also overlaps with other ranged classes like Mages or Warlocks, who bring comparable damage along with additional utility. This loss of identity has made playing a Hunter in PvP far less enjoyable and rewarding.

Hunter is the class that i wanted to play and PvP the aspect i want to experience, those are simply not enjoyable anymore, so i prefer to quit TWOW overall.

Goodbye, have fun.

Hunter is the class that i wanted to play and PvP the aspect i want to experience, those are simply not enjoyable anymore, so i prefer to quit TWOW overall.

Goodbye, have fun.

subject: Mongoose Bite macro for nubies
content_md:
Hello
Just found out how to use mongoose bite more efficient. Maybe someone will find it useful. Maybe its not new info but i am only learning how to play hunter and want to share

> Mongoose Bite no longer requires you to dodge to use it, now deals 60% Weapon Damage in addition to its current flat damage and resets your auto-attack swing timer.

Ingame tooltip doesnt say it but mongoose resets timer indeed. If you start combat with casting mongoose you start swing timer without autoattack hit

I played warrior years ago and know hint how to use Slam. Just tuned it for mongoose. So here is how to:
 1) Download addon SP_SwingTimer

> /run if not _a then for i=1,72 do if IsAttackAction(i) then _a=i end end end if not IsCurrentAction(_a)then UseAction(_a)end if st_timer>UnitAttackSpeed"player"*0.8 then CastSpellByName"Mongoose Bite" end

and just spam it

author: Rinarch
subject: Re: Battle Shout, Blessing of Might, and Strength of Earth improvements
content_md:
I don't care much for PvP so I can't really speak to that aspect of the game.  To me that is a whole different game within the larger game and it requires it's own set of balancing and rules.  S

urvival wrecks MM anytime there is more then 3 targets and still outshines us at <3 targets.  But that is by design, so it is what it is.  The small bump in DPS from benefiting from BoMight and Battle shout would just make the inverse true for single target boss fights.  Right now Survival is on the heels of a MM hunter in a single target fight and I believe the gap should be a bit larger considering how much a difference there is in AoE pack damage between the 2 specs.

We don't "outrange" most mechanics, that is a fallacy.

Sure we do have it safer but that is because of the fact that range do not need to clump together to do damage like melee should be.  The disadvantage to this is, as a ranged player, the moment a mechanic targets me my DPS plummets as there is not much in my toolkit to keep damage going as I move.  Most mechanics don't allow studder stepping, arcane shot does jackshit for damage, and at my current haste level I have all off .5 seconds to move before i need to stop and fire again if I want to keep my dps rolling.  For most mechanics that means I'm getting hit unless I drop all damage and get out.  Melee on the other hand get targeted as a group more, because it is a target rich environment.  But they can keep dps rolling while moving out of danger for most mechanics.  That's the trade off, A playstyle where you are more likely to get targeted and hence need to be more on the go to keep damage up vs one where prep and encounter knowledge can benefit you as you find better spots to be.  Knowing that if you are the target of an attack your DPS is going to drop to survive.

There is very little benefit to having self sufficiency in a group/raid environment so I would definitely trade of better buff scaling for that, especially in the damage department.  It's not like MM hunters are kitting mobs around to kill them, we tag them, run away and the FD when the raid is ready to kill that target.  So I would gladly do a little less personal unbuffed damage to be able to benefit for a wide array of raid buffs.

You do bring up a good point about the totem massively benefiting the other melee as well.  The agi group is a good compromise.

author: Rinarch
subject: Re: Battle Shout, Blessing of Might, and Strength of Earth improvements
content_md:
I understand the value of ranged DPS, I think where we differ in opinion is the downside that offsets that value.  Personally I don't believe the classes scalability to buffs should enter in the equation as part of that downside.

Melee is in a target rich environment for raid mechanics, so they are continually keep up DPS while on the move to dodge said mechanics.  A melee's position is always behind  and slightly to the side  of the boss, for every encounter.
Their focus is not the larger picture of the boss arena for the most part, it is their smaller melee arena which is usually in a constant state of flux because of the constant disruption of boss mechanics.

Ranged on the other hand are rarely required to clump together, quite the opposite we usually have a wide spread across the boss arena.  So larger movements in our position cost us DPS.  Sure we might have an instant or 2 that we can fire off to keep DPS up slightly but part of our design is to know how an encounter is going to play out in terms of the use of area in the arena and position accordingly to maximize DPS.

Our scalability in terms of how buffs operate for our class really have no part in this balance between melee and ranged DPS.

author: Rinarch
subject: Re: Battle Shout, Blessing of Might, and Strength of Earth improvements
content_md:
None of that has anything to do with how MM as a spec currently scales with the attack power buffs.  MM hunters have always been a crit focused damage dealer, that is what the whole spec centers around.  Always has, and always will.  But the downside to that is crit is a negative sloping parabolic scaling attribute.  The more you have the less valuable it becomes.  The diminishing point really starts to hit hard when crit drops below a .9% damage increase per 1% crit.  That point is already being reached in Naxx gear with raid consumes.  We will need the scalability of attack power buffs to stay competitive in the damage scene.  The Trueshot aura change is a step in the right direction for sure.  But without a way via gear to get a substantial amount of haste or armor pen MM damage is going to fall off.  Unrestricting these AP buffs from melee only is an easy solution to that problem.

If your raid is having issues, you swapping from survival to MM isn't going to fix them.  That is just a cope.  If you as a melee aren't getting hit by mechanics then you swapping to a ranged spec isn't going to make you get hit less by mechanics.  Now if your raid is way to melee heavy then sure swapping to ranged helps but that brings in a whole other aspect of the survival thing.

Why did we create another melee class in an already melee heavy era of the game?  But that is a whole other topic and quite frankly that cat is out of the bag isn never going back so no point in having the discussion.

Starting in patch 3.0.2 (pre-Wrath of the Lich King), Blizzard gave hunter pets a passive called Avoidance.

- Avoidance (Rank 1): Reduces AOE damage taken by 75% from non-player sources.
- Avoidance (Rank 2): Increased that reduction to 90%, introduced in patch 3.1.0 (Ulduar).
The whole point was to negate boss mechanics meant for raid members to dodge without unduly punishing hunters.

Honestly, this seems like a better (and more balanced) fix then removing the pet altogether.

Another potential avenue might be to apply avoidance only while mend pet is active. This way it turns the passive into an active and makes mend pet more beneficial, the avoidance more reactive, and less of a "I don't even have to consider the consequences of ignoring my pet."

author: Akos1896
subject: Survival tree theory-craft
content_md:
Hey!

Wanted to create a theory-craft for the survival tree, giving it the 'enhancement shaman treatment', meaning that its goal is both to serve a melee DPS and a (dungeon) tank build now.
It is not a suggestion but I found this idea very interesting so I gave it a shot.

It's not on the tree but I imagine that in this world Aspect of the Monkey also gives a threat modifier next to the plus dodge. Melee uses Wolf anyway, Monkey is mostly used sometimes in PVP and in some open world fights, usually if the pet is down. Threat shouldn't really affect things there.
I also 'imagined' that hunters have some sort of taunt here, didn't elaborate on it on the tree itself.
Changing between aspects eats up a GCD.

Highlighted any talent I changed or added.
Removed Survivalist. While it's cool for tanks, didn't want to overload the tree with talents and it gave me 5TPs to work with.
My core idea was to make some talents 'modular ones', doing slightly different things with Aspect of the Wolf and Aspect of the Monkey. Wolf becoming 'the' melee DPS aspect, Monkey is used for tanks.

<https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/tree/bwFOSKAtNj>

 **Some explanation behind the changes:**

 * Swift Reflexes: Made it a 3TP talent. DPS hunter gets +1% haste, tank also has +1% parry. Small change. Wanted to give this +1% parry since hunters have no block but didn't want to go over 3% with the haste buff.
 * Removed Survivalist, replaced it with primal Mitigation (3TP). Wanted to give a soul link look-alike for tank's mitigation. Of course made it worse since we are far from being at the bottom of the tree. At the same time, gave DPS some threat management here. In my experience, melee hunter can go a bit over the top with threat, unless they cancel their rotation regularly to use threat-reduction strikes.
 * Carve out, Strike Command in. I felt that most hunter players complained about carve, feeling weird. Trap takes care of the AoE damage anyway, wanted to replace it with something else, which also has a pet-theme. I really felt like pet-combo melee attacks were lacking from this tree, wanted to make one. Using Wolf aspect it gives a nice buff to the pet, too. With Monkey, it has a threat modifier to facilitate tanking.
 * Rapid Strikes also reducing Strike Command's CS by 1 sec. I imagined that talent to have around 10-12 Sec CD by default.
 * Killer Instinct -> Survival Instinct: Gave the +crit for everyone but closed the + damage behind the Wolf aspect. In case of Monkey, you get a buff for damage mitigation. As it stands, hunter mitigation is still really bad. Didn't want to make them too tanky, would go against the theme. Instead, reduced the damage taken by crits. F.ex. with this 20% crit damage reduction a crit with 150% damage would deal 120% damage to them. The goal was to prevent too big spikes in the HP.
 * Lightning Reflexes: Made it modular, too. Agility increase is for everyone. Extra attack power is locked behind Wolf, Monkey gets 10% of agility as defense instead.
 * Lastly, added a new capstone talent: Aspect Mastery. Wolf grants some of your attack power to your pet. 20% was a made up number, I happily change it if needed. Monkey gives a big armor increase based on your agility. 300% seems excessive but I can accept it as a capstone talent. Hunter agi usually goes around 500 at raids if done well. It means 1500 armor which is a mediocre late-game shield at best so I think 300% is all right.

Track Hidden's Stealth Detection value is 30 -- considering every 5 equates to +1 Levels, that is tantamount to being six Levels above potential victims (on top of Minimap display when seen). F.ex. L50 VS L50 with Track Hidden, it's like L56 VS L50.

It must be noted that it is for Stealth only, not Invisibility.

Any +Stealth modifiers like Talents, Equipment and Enchantments are to also be kept in mind (Feral, Sub, Cloak Enchantment, etc.).

Easy to test would be by checking with two Characters that have a six-Level difference and absolutely nothing else of the above in effect; if Track Hidden then does not give the same results as though you were six Levels in difference while on, then it clearly has some issue here.

author: Terryleelolorz
subject: Re: Leveling as Survival?
content_md:
Sure, it’s definitely viable. The Survival talent tree has been significantly enhanced on Turtle server. With the buffs to Aspect of the Wolf and the new talents, it’s a great choice for leveling. In my opinion, while Survival hunters still might not level as easily as BM hunters, they have their own unique advantages:
 1. They have the highest Agility and Stamina among all three specs.
 2. They can use traps in combat to escape, and the traps also have immobilization effects (with talent support), as well as Deterrence and Improved Feign Death.
 3. They have some AOE capabilities.
 4. Unlike traditional specs that rarely get attacked by mobs and may end up with insufficient defense skill experience, Survival hunters are like melee fighters. Their defense skills can always be kept at the maximum level, making them less likely to be stunned by mobs.

author: Barwat1
subject: Re: New player question - Survival hunter spec
content_md:
Survival is far from a meme spec, it is performing to the highest of levels with one survival hunter getting to the top 10 of best hunter dps in naxx. It is definitely a front pack runner, with dps on par with other top dogs.

For raid utility, they are very limited, the use of traps during combat allows you to guarantee some CC like frost trap, but doing so shafts your dps as your damage relies on fire traps going off.
It's very unreliable to tranq as a melee hunter as you need to move out of the deadzone to use it, lowering your dps and unless you have a perfect timer for enrages, you end up putting your tanks at risk. Their pulling ability is also getting nerfed because no range talent.

For raid spot, that depends on the guild and how they value raw dps or if traps are really necessary for an encounter (which is almost never, or can be reliably done by 1-2 MM hunter if you don't get unlucky resists on FD).

MM hunter brings party-wide (not raid-wide) aura that scales with current AP, in our last raid, a feral friend got more than 200AP out of the trueshot aura which is a big deal. I'd say the main difference between MM and survival is the aoe damage and overall raid damage. While MM shines on single target bosses and lacks aoe in general, survival more than makes up for that and is one of the best aoe class rivaling warlocks and mages while having pretty much comparable single target.

An additional point for solo players that like farming instances, open world, ... Survival is much better than MM because at some point your gear just gets too strong and your pet will never keep aggro on you ever again, so being able to just smack people in melee range makes hunter great at grinding and the added AoE to  the hunter kit opens a lot of new farms.

Ultimately it comes down to preference, the rotation and play style of survival is very fun and having this option is nice. Personally I'm gonna try and push this spec in the newest raid and see how it can perform. They also buffed dual wielding as a hunter so there's that to look forward to when I get decent one handers.

author: Steakhouse
subject: Re: New player question - Survival hunter spec
content_md:
Surv's real claim to fame is how flexible it is. You can do decent damage at all ranges and for any number of targets ; its ace in the hole is its utility though. Being able to Freeze Trap or Frost Trap in combat is incredibly useful and will save wipes many a times. This falls off a bit in raids since most bosses are immune to any form of CC, but in dungeons and in the world it's a godsend; plus many raid encounters are add-heavy, where your combat ice traps will be very very very useful.

For soloing I've found BM to be better though, because you pull aggro off your pet quite easily and are too close to kite effectively. Plus you want to be in melee to be dealing max damage anyways.

author: Amyloriley
subject: Re: Mod to see actual happiness value?
content_md:
Not a direct answer, but if you feed your pet, you will see the buff in your combat log (so not general chat) increasing the pet's happiness.

Depending on the level of the food (the level of the zone you can find the food in as an enemy drop) and the level of the pet, it will increase either by 35, by 17, or by 8, every 2 seconds for 20 seconds, totaling 350, 170, or 80 happiness. At a given moment, your pet will be full and eating food won't increase happiness anymore. You can still feed a pet though. So, look closely at your combat log!

The buff disappears after 20 seconds, or when your pet enters combat, whichever happens first.

There are 6 ranks of Loyalty. Higher Loyalty means your pet can stays happy longer without topping up food. Loyalty has an xp component and a time component. To gain a new rank of Loyalty, your pet needs to gain combat xp worth about 5% of your xp bar; and some time needs to pass. 0 minutes to reach Loyalty 2, 30 minutes in Loyalty 2 to reach Loyalty 3, and so on...

Happiness will drop over time.

 - Standing around doing nothing (like in cities) makes it drop, reported to be 50 happiness over 6 minutes.
 - Dismissing makes it lose 50 happiness, but then you can stand around for as long as you want without a further penalty.
 - Walking out of range of your pet makes it lose 10 happiness. This includes using the Stay command while you walk away, and is often used in place of the Dismiss Pet button because of the reduced happiness loss.
 - Mounting does disappear your pet, but it does not reduce happiness.
 - When your pet dies, reports say it loses 350 happiness.

You can also look for WoW Classic for information. Lastly, [petopia](<https://www.wow-petopia.com/classic/>) is your friend, even if it doesn't include foxes and serpents (TurtleWoW-only families). (
[embed: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1NbwgI9kuGvAXlfD-tpoXZ2VMwtsUBwPMhI1yrQKgeaU/preview#gid=0]

- When your pet dies, reports say it loses 350 happiness.

author: Steakhouse
subject: Ideas to buff Improved Hunter's Mark
content_md:
I know Marks is performing well, and that there are cases for speccing Imp Hunter's Mark as is, but it's kindof a boring talent that doesn't feel very good to grab, spending multiple points in giving a few extra RAP points is meh. Here are some ideas on how to improve it.

 1) Make it interact with Hit chance

This works well with the aiming scope visual and would make it a wonderful debuff to apply to bosses: "Increases chance to hit the target by 1%" at max rank. If this is too strong, simply improving the Hunter's chance to hit is great (and perhaps their pet's !)

 2) Make a % of the ranged AP bonus also apply to melee AP

This is what TBC did. I think it's pretty self explanatory. Again if this is too strong, could be limited to the Hunter and their pet.

author: Gattare
subject: Some questions about technical details of survival hunter
content_md:
I have recently leveled a Survival Hunter to 40 and I am having a lot of fun but I also have some questions.
 1、Does Hunter's Mark's attack power-boosting effect work on melee combat?
 2、Which weapon is better for survival hunters, two-handed or dual wielding? Should I consider weapon damage or agility more?
 3、I completely forgo ranged weapons and equip throwing weapons, which I find saves a lot of inventory space, but I doubt this will change later on. Because I don't know whether the skill of range weapons will still be important to us in high level.
 4、I find that survival hunters make so much aggro that my pets can't hold mobs most of the time. Should I give up tank pets and switch to my Broken Tooth?
 5、Does Survival Hunter have significant mana issues in the end game?

author: zer0g3
subject: Re: Some questions about technical details of survival hunter
content_md:
> **Gattare wrote: Wed May 14, 2025 9:59 pm**
> I have recently leveled a Survival Hunter to 40 and I am having a lot of fun but I also have some questions.
>  1、Does Hunter's Mark's attack power-boosting effect work on melee combat?
>  2、Which weapon is better for survival hunters, two-handed or dual wielding? Should I consider weapon damage or agility more?
>  3、I completely forgo ranged weapons and equip throwing weapons, which I find saves a lot of inventory space, but I doubt this will change later on. Because I don't know whether the skill of range weapons will still be important to us in high level.
>  4、I find that survival hunters make so much aggro that my pets can't hold mobs most of the time. Should I give up tank pets and switch to my Broken Tooth?
>  5、Does Survival Hunter have significant mana issues in the end game?

 1. No. The ability specifies *ranged attack power*
 2. For now, Two-handed is by far the better choice, dual wield was buffed recently, but probably needs a little more to be truly comparable.

 3. You are going to need a standard ranged weapon such as bow/crossbow or gun for the end game. One of the cool things about Melee Hunt is that unlike a Rogue or a Warrior that mostly carry their ranged weapons for passive stats and the situational utility. A Hunter is still a Hunter, even specialized for close combat, your ranged playstyle remains fully available whenever you need it. Albeit significantly lower damage. There are several encounters, however, where you'd rather be alive with half the DPS.

 4. Yes, forget about your pet holding aggro as Survival. Screechers are a popular choice for this build.
 5. Used to have *significant* mana issues before they reduced the costs. Now it's just *mana issues.*

author: SvenS2
subject: Re: Survival talent : stinging nettle
content_md:
It sounds odd on paper, but in practice it makes sense.

First case is, it's applied for free when using Mongoose bite/Fire Traps, so there's no cost downside to the overlapping application.

Fire Traps also apply the DoT, and the target(s) may not be your main target, so the additional duration comes into play.

It's also a way to reserve some mana, as you're not required to re-apply the dot immediately when Mongoose bite comes out of CD.

The increased duration make it more effective for PvP, where the opponent can get some distance away from you, allowing you to still apply some damage to them.
---
I understand your concern with it however. In a boss fight, where you spam Mongoose bite, you effectively gain only 1 extra second of Serpent Sting damage from this Talent. Given its other utilities, I think the talent is fine right now

author: Atreidon
subject: Re: Survival talent : stinging nettle
content_md:
While this is squarely in the "not an actual problem" category, its squarely in the needs tweaking category.

In classic, if you reapply a dot, you reset its ticks. Casting mongoose bite every 4 seconds means you never get the value from the second talent point. And despite mongoose bite being up 100% of the time, it only ticks every 4 seconds. And you likely further eat ticks by using immo trap.

Removing stinging nettle from mongoose bite and putting it at full duration on the firetraps would be a solution, but that has the downside of omegabuffing survivals already good aoe.

Alternatively an application like deadly poison could help where the ticktimer of seepent sting doesnt restart. Either by both abilities adding x time to the duration instead of reapplying it. That might especially be an option if the AoE is deemed to be a bit over the top currently

author: Zogtog
subject: Death of a Hunter
content_md:
The young huntress crept silently in the silence of the night to the cave and carefully, slightly touching the skin at the entrance, crept inside. In the depths, an old orc sat hunched over by the fire. His once powerful hands shook slightly when he added another log to the fire, but even now it was clear that he noticed her presence. Slowly lowering the unfinished fire trap to the floor, he stuck one hand under his bed.

 - You bypassed all my traps, so it really is that I am already quite bad. Why did you come?

The elf came closer, but did not sit down by the fire, remaining in the shadows.

 - I fulfilled my part of the prophecy, whoever tracks down the Great Pathfinder will be able to become part of the family. I need your knowledge, hunter, I want to be like you, to hit a squirrel in the eye from a hundred yards away, to talk to animals and run faster than the wind, luring the most terrible monsters of this world into traps.

 - Go away, I don't take any more students!

 - Am I right? Are you the one they told legends about? Show me your Rhok'delar, Longbow of the Ancient Keepers, and I will swear an oath of allegiance to our cause!

 - No more deeds! No more oaths! No more hunters and family! The gods have cursed us and deprived us of our eyes! - the old orc screamed, tears streaming down his wrinkled cheeks - We don't hunt anymore, we only survive now...

The orc threw off the blanket. In his hand, instead of the legendary bow, was an old, jagged two-handed axe.
