author: Cabum
subject: Marksmanship is not in a good spot
content_md:
MM falls behind as a pure dps class. Here are some points I experience raiding MM for 2 years, and from others hunters.

 1. Mediocre single target dps, and very poor aoe solutions.

 2. Shots scale with spellpower, while survival tree has the option to change trap scaling to attackpower.

 2. New tier 3.5 set does not fit MM spec. Increased haste on quickshots by 5% and the heavy amount of %hit on gear are more suited for melee survival spec.

 3. Lack of synergy with other melees. Windfury, strength totem, battle shout, and blessing of might. Having a % from attack power to affect range attack power could make those buffs more relevant.

 4. Consume buffs that do not affect range attack power. Exp.: Elixir of Demonslaying, ele sharp stones, engi chicken.

 5. Dull talents added to MM from cc2, extra shot and bleeds. Having a % from range ap on bleeds, like the new Lacerate spell for surv, would feel more consistent. Removing the extrashot talent and let windfury work on range hits sounds fun, but maybe to strong.

C&P from what I posted under the 1.8 changes.

 - Aimshot, another core hunter spell, useless in both pvp and pve. Long cast time, hits like a noodle. Not even a change to apply mortal strike for arena. Tons of ways to make it viable, no change.
 - Serpent sting, no AP scaling. Useless.
 - Arcane shot, no AP scaling. Useless.
 - Volley, no AP scaling. Useless.
 - Viper sting, nerfed, arena is going up. Useless.
 - We dont even get silencing shot in a world where an arcane mage can one tap us with 1k crits through a fucking wall, los while casting AM.

Hunter received 0 QOL in terms of resource management or kiting abilities, no wotlk disengage, how are the devs thinking BM/MM will be able to do anything in arena? author: Webecca
subject: Re: Marksmanship is not in a good spot
content_md:
I wouldn't say that MM is in a particularly terrible spot. It's not great, around middle of the pack dps. In good conditions and good hands it gets slightly better than that. It doesn't necessarily need a major overhaul to be good, but it's fair to expect more than nothing.
What gets frustrating for some MM players is that one can perceive a bias in spec design within the class. One would expect that the designers would have seen the clear performance gap that has existed since the mongoose bite rework a while back. MM loses out in every type of encounter. Sustained, bursty, aoe, single target.
It certainly doesn't help that the new raid has more aoe and add phases than any previous raid, where the gap is largest.
And yet time and again we see more survival buffs and QoL, while MM appears to be forgotten.
Having 2 dead points in the second/third tiers, haste/gcd cap issues just with its own class buffs, certain consumables and buffs not affecting ranged shots, just to name a few.
Strangely, juju flurry is about to affect spell casting speed in 1.18, but for unclear reasons a change to demonslaying elixir is inappropriate.
The implication isn't that this is maliciously done to force someone's favorite spec to the top or put down another. But personal bias happens and can be distracting from balanced design.
To end on a positive note, the upcoming BM rework and new pet abilities are very exciting! I hope MM can receive another look with fresh eyes as well.

author: SvenS2
subject: Re: Don't Touch Bestial Wrath
content_md:
I'm neutral leaning towards positive on the change, and here's my reasoning.

On one hand, for PvE people mostly skip it in favor of Improved Steady shot, likewise in PvP scenarios for Scatter Shot. So apart from leveling and some PvP players, the ability is not part of your usual rotation.

That being said, what we're getting as replacements does not look half bad. Kill Command has a much shorter CD, making it more useful in PvP scenarios. As for DPS output, the addition of Coordinated Assault and Baited Shot make up for it, and will probably end up providing more dps overall if you go deep BM, which was probably the goal. With Kill Command you can also safely stay at 2 value points in Frenzy, since you'll have more crit sources. With the change overall, BM hunters are given more reasons to go deep into their talent tree.

On paper it sounds fine, but we'll just have to wait for the patch to land and see

My main problem with the rework is that it trades an ability which had an identity for specific situations (burst and cc resistenc) and a cooldown so it was actually good in said situations.
For another set of bells and whistles to do dps. Your pet being cced is basically a nonfactor with it being freed from all ccs every 15 seconds just by doing your default rotation.
And then its that, just replace your old one button rotation with 3. But the end result is pretty much the same. Just straight up single target dps. So you trade an ability that can be used right or wrong for a braindead set of abilities.

Can BM - or hunter in general - benefit from being less locked into only steady shot for his rotation? Absolutely. Steady shot has been a massive downgrade for the fun of playing hunter. Despite making it perform substantially better.

But this doesnt need to come at the cost of the one single ability that is really associated with the spec.

This is really what pisses me off about this change. author: Bigsmerf
subject: Re: Don't Touch Bestial Wrath
content_md:
> **Illyria wrote: Tue Aug 05, 2025 5:02 am**
> I understand that the take kill command removes control, but does not give immunity. Bestial wrath removes control and gives immunity.

That's kinda the issue though.

Having two abilities that break CC, with one of them granting full immunity, is definitely a bit problematic. Because that isn't even taking the hunter into account. You'd be spending one CC and GCD on the pet, only for it to escape, only to waste another CC, only for it to escape again and become completely immune to any form of control. All while you've got the hunter themselves to deal with. This could be heavily oppressive towards casters, or melees not yet in range. Getting dazed by the pet while you're chasing means you're in big trouble.

I'm assuming Turtle either A) thought that just removing Bestial Wrath outright would fix this issue and completely ignored the other problem. That problem being this ability has been a part of BM since the dawn of time and removing it would be taking away a part of its identity/flavor. Or B) Already came up with the big brain idea of replacing Bestial wrath only to remember ''Oh right we gotta give pets their CC resistance back'' and just slapped it on Kill Command and called it a day.

Absolute genius.

author: Hctwowfan
subject: Re: Hunter Pet skill Trainer
content_md:
> **Mercer92 wrote: Tue Aug 12, 2025 5:41 am**
> im a level 12 human hunter i got the pet tamer quest done, everytime I tame a pet it has -4 skill points and I cant use the basic abilities no growl nothing and it keeps staying in rebellious level 1 and nothing I do works it doesnt matter if I reset the pet talent tree or level him up nothing changes

Your pet comes with negative training points (tp) because it has an ability already (most likely claw 1).

Your pet has a max of 300 tp at lvl 60. The math is:
pet lvl x (loyalty - 1) = tp

at 60:
 60 x (6 - 1) = 300

Your pet right after taming has (independent of pet level):
pet lvl x (1 - 1) = 0 - cost of known abilities = -4

If you understand the math you'll see that leveling your pet will still provide zero tp if the loyalty is at 1. Increasing the loyalty will provide an amount of tp equal to your pet lvl.

If you want to increase your tp, you need to increase the loyalty. Loyalty only increases if your pets happiness is green or yellow (feed the pet) AND if your pet gains experience from killing mobs. Standing in town with a green happiness pet for 10 days won't do anything for the loyalty.

subject: Hunter gold farming after speedrunning to 60 on new server
content_md:
Hello everyone! :) I'm new to Turtle WoW, but not to WoW.  I've been playing TWoW for about a week, so please forgive my ignorance of it.

I've had fun speedrunning to 60 on several classic and vanilla servers. I was relaxing and leveling some characters while experiencing TWoW for the first time, but then they announced the new server launch on August 17th, and I thought... why not give it a try?

I'll play a BM Hunter, and I'm pretty sure I won't be the first on the server to hit 60, but I will reach 60 pretty fast. But that's not the main point.

Since I'm new to Turtle WoW, I'm not sure what the best way is to take advantage of having less competition for farming spots (or other ways to make gold). On a regular vanilla server, I'd probably go mining or herbalism + skinning, then head straight to farm Devilsaurs. Later, when it gets crowded, I'd move to Maraudon and/or DM Tribute solo runs.

But on a Turtle WoW server, I have no idea if that's the best approach.

author: Bigsmerf
subject: Re: Melee (Survival) Hunter
content_md:
Call me crazy, but, melee hunter was already viable before CC2 made it a real supported thing.

As in: Your raid/group wouldn't wipe to some hidden mechanic preventing a hunter from entering melee range.

Brief fit of rambling aside- yes. Melee hunter performs good (from what I'm told) and is extremely fun. You'll have issues with levelling early on as baseline ability support (only having raptor strike until 20 something) is pretty lacking, but past the 20s it'll start to shape up and become a decent way to level. You're tankier/more slippery with talents, so your pet not being able to keep threat isn't an issue very often, and damage can get pretty high. If you're going for efficiency BM is still king, but, I had good fun with survival. The best part is you don't need to commit too much to one build since survival scales really well with agility which is a bread and butter hunter stat.

So, to summarize:

Not very good early levelling. Likely better off playing BM until you get a significant amount of melee throughput stuff. Mongoose bite and wolf aspect are important.

Gearing is simple, and straightforward, not clashing with other hunter specs making for easy switching whenever you desire.

Damage performance is great at endgame, with especially strong cleave rivalling if not eclipsing warriors, but there's a significant lack of utility/special support.

Traps count as spells, so you might lack heavily in the damage department in early raids, where fire resist is just leaking out the ass of every trash mob and boss. Hopefully this is fixed.

Very rare occurrence, but sometimes traps bug out and just won't drop. This tends to happen back to back when it does, but like I said, very rare. It's possible this is getting fixed, but I'm just guessing.

This talent build likely isn't optimal, but, it's what I've got. You could also go down MM for improved stings since stinging nettle applies serpent sting, but I feel like your pet living longer and doing more damage will see more use than ranged abilities (as a MELEE hunter lawl) costing a bit less mana. Also, serpent sting's damage isn't very high to begin with. Pets have multiple forms of throughput with autoattacks, and abilities.

[https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/hunter?p ... TAbIQoBAA=](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/hunter?points=FoAAAoAIAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAFQCYBJTAbIQoBAA=)

Also, warning. Your pet will NOT hold threat. I personally haven't tried using a bat, but my cat couldn't tank for shit the entire time I was playing survival. The trade-off for this is you can soak up damage better, and slowing down on damage so your buddy CAN tank for you is helpful when you want to minimize taking damage. Especially at levels where you're not wearing mail.

author: Atreidon
subject: Re: Bug on taming pet and skill points
content_md:
Your pet gets 1 training point per loyality level per level.
So at loyality 6 (best friend) and level 60 you have 300.

At low level and low loyality you have none or almost none of these.
But your pet innately knows either claw or bite. Thats costs points to know. Which is taken away from your points. Since you have less training points than what your pet has in abilities you are negative.

All working as intended. Just feed your pet well and loyality (and points) will rise

author: Hctwowfan
subject: Re: Bug on taming pet and skill points
content_md:
Formula to calculate pet's TP:
Pet level x (Loyalty - 1) - cost of pet skills = remaining TP

Max pet:
 60 x (6 - 1) = 300 tp

Your pet:
 10 x (1 - 1) - 4 = -4 tp

once it increases loyalty (assuming same level pet):
 10 x (2 - 1) - 4 = 6 tp

Pet loyalty only increases if you keep your pet above unhappy AND only increases if the pet gains xp. So standing around in town and keeping your pet happy won't increase its loyalty, because the pet doesn't gain any xp.

I somewhat agree with this.

Here are the changes I’d like to see:

Ferocity Talent: Change it from a 5-point talent to a 3-point talent.
Make it give +5% crit per talent point.

New Talent (Beast Mastery tree): Add a talent that makes guns more effective for BM hunters.
 2 talents.

Baited Shot Rework:
Instead of doing 125% weapon damage, have it scale with ranged attack power or deal a % of the pet’s attack damage.
Instead of only triggering when the pet attacks, make it so both the hunter’s attacks and the pet’s attacks can restore focus.
Keep the same trigger cooldown, but give the hunter and pet separate cooldowns.
Casting Baited Shot should put Steady Shot on cooldown.

Of course, the numbers would need fine-tuning to avoid damage being too high or too low. The real benefit of these changes is that they create two distinct playstyles: faster weapons becoming the optimal choice for Beast Mastery and slower weapons remaining stronger for Marksmanship. This separation would make each spec feel more unique and rewarding to play.

author: Mekk
subject: Re: Beast Mastery Rework [ Tank and DPS ]
content_md:
The only thing that comes to mind is in WotLK, they added a Pet Talent that lowered the chance your pet could be critically hit by 3/6%, making it uncritable by bosses.  I do not, however, recall if this is required for Classic.

Other than that, I always enjoyed OTing with my Hunter.  Of course, having a guild that supported my crazy nonsense was also quite helpful. LOL  It wasn't as bad as it sounds, and even came in clutch OTing some adds in a raid more than once (happened in Gruul's Lair on more than one occasion).  Many 5-mans were doable up through LK (I stopped playing early Cata), and I did some OTing in a few raids in BC/LK, which was hilarious and fun; a little chaotic at times, but never caused any wipes or anything.  I recall having a few macros set up for some better pet control.  The biggest issue I recall having with Pet Tank is lack of solid AoE aggro, so if a fight had a bunch of adds I had to assume the role of not-quite-MT while the real MT dealt with the adds.  I also recall there being a few bosses in which there were some issues, but I think those were mostly due to a combination of boss movement (esp fliers), Pet AI, and room geometry; but that was also a long time ago. :D  (*EDIT: I recall someone made a post about them MTing Icecrown as a Hunter. Of course, I believe this was after most of the guild was already geared out.  Still, I think that would have made for a fun challenge*).

Personally, I've always wanted to be able to fight in melee alongside my pet, like Rexxar, trading aggro back and forth using a melee Distracting Strike and Intimidation, while also swapping between a Melee DPS Aspect and Monkey Aspect for Evasion; but I'm not really sure how you'd Talent that w/o making BM the melee spec. LOL

subject: Lacerate dot vs. Immo trap dot scalling
content_md:
First of all, I like the new Lacerate talent and its interaction (available after a player critically hits). What I do not like is the disparity between Immo trap fire damage and lacerate. When you go deep into the survival tree (at lease 31 points) your immo trap fire dot starts to do some rally nice damage because it scales from MAP. author: Hctwowfan
subject: Re: Lacerate dot vs. Immo trap dot scalling
content_md:
Sorry for the semi necro but Lacerate has to be the most awful ability ever.

You need to invest 2 talent points to get the ability. You can only use it after a crit. It costs a substantial amount of mana. Lacerate is underpowered af for its cost.

Let's say you had 1000 melee ap (which is already asking a lot tbh). You deal 35% = 350 damage before damage mitigation, best case if you're positioned correctly you gain another +10% damage = 385 and the bleed then ticks for a total of 77 damage. Did you lacerate the fingertip of your opponent? And on top of all that it can simply be dodged or parried.

Compare that to Overpower. Needs no talent points to get access to the ability. Needs 2 tp to increase crit to +50%. Costs very little rage compared to average rage cost. Can only be used after the opponent dodges, cannot be blocked, parried or dodged. Deals substantial damage.

Lacerate, for an ability this deep in the survival tree, with mana cost, requiring to crit the opponent first to use it, can be dodged and parried, deals way too little damage.

Either buff the damage, buff the bleed damage or make it baseline and not requiring talent points to get access to. Or give it a fancy additional effect, like mongoose bite and raptor strike refresh the bleed or deal additional damage to a bleeding target. In its current form, Lacerate is just useless.

author: Sarthrethal
subject: Surv Hunter after 1.18
content_md:
Greetings!
I want to raise the topic of nerfing hunters in the survival spec.
At first, if we remember, the main nerf of damage was through reducing the bonus to 2 main melee abilities from 20 percent and 20 flat to 10 percent and flat, respectively, which was already a significant nerf of overall damage for the survival spec.

 **1st version:** Vicious Strikes: Now reduces the cooldown of Raptor Strike and Mongoose Bite by 0.5/1 second but the damage increase is reduced from 10/20% weapon damage and 10/20 flat damage to 5/10% weapon damage and 5/10 flat damage.

 **2nd version:** Vicious Strikes: No longer increases Raptor Strike and Mongoose Bite damage.

In contrast, the survival spec was given a new skill, **Lacerate**.
Which, according to the description, looked very weak, and it no longer covered the loss of promised dps.
However, before the release, the bonus damage to mongoose and raptor strike was completely removed and two key abilities lost their identity in this spec, since the only buff left was a 1-second cooldown reduction.
The damage of these abilities became basic.
It turns out that MM and BM deal the same amount of damage with these abilities.
Which hits the identity of the survival spec hunter.
Which now only has "improved traps", and let's be honest, fire traps, without the talents of the survival spec - absolutely unused and useless.

The new skill lacerate is very weak.
 35% of AP is a very weak primary damage. With a raid gear with 2k AP - we have ~600-700 damage from the ability, which is still cut by armor. Where there are no critical value multipliers, we have ~900-1000 (taking into account the modifier of a blow to the back or side) damage from a crit.

The DOT from this ability has just a meme damage, 20% of the damage inflicted, if we take conditionally 1000, then the DOT will be 200 in 8 seconds, in a good raid composition and full dps chemistry - was 35-37 damage per tick.
We will also keep quiet about a ton of mobs and bosses with immunity to bleeding.
Damage from Dot - you can simply not take into account.

Benchmark was taken in BWL, in a good raid composition, with a shaman in the party, and full dps chemistry and full T2 gear.
If before I could compete with mages in full T2 and retpals, DC priests, ENH shamans as a main survival hunter, now the final outgoing damage has fallen by more than 25%, with all the raid multipliers and bonuses. 600-650k damage when before this amount was 850-900k.
Now I don't even have the opportunity to somehow get close to my mates. Since I did everything the same as before, and it is difficult to do better, maybe 5-7% with lucky crits and slack of my guys, but the gap of 20-25% remains, and it is no longer possible to overcome it.

I repeat, the comparison is with players who have the same level of equipment.

Lacerate is at the very bottom of the dps meter, it is lower than a **PET** that is not strengthened by any talent from the BM tree.
With 30+% crit in melee. It procs on CD and it was used on CD.
Remember, BWL is one of the worst raids for pets.
This ability is also very expensive in mana.
Surv Hunter already had problems with mana, now he becomes OOM in just 35-45 seconds, even with a paladin and a sham in the group. If we take content for 10 - 5 people, and there is no sham paladin, you drink more often than any class.
If you wanted to tie this class with the use of mana potions and teas, congratulations, you did it.

As a result, the survival spec has become extremely ineffective, yes, you can run with it, but you will not be able to give similar efficiency to other classes. To give out damage, you need to do more, but you give out significantly less. THIS IS ABSOLUTELY NOT FUN.
Satisfaction and reward for the game for this spec has disappeared.
It would not have been very common spec, but now even being a fan of the spec, I am seriously thinking about reroll to another character.

I am not against the first version of reducing damage from 20 to 10 percent and flat. Since you will no longer be competent with other specs.
Lacerate, for such a mana cost, needs to be changed, in its current form this skill is not worth it.
Perhaps increasing the primary damage from 35 to 65% and the damage dot from 20 to 60% will make this skill at least somewhat useful.
Or the ability to stack bleeding up to three times.

Thank you!

author: Sikarii
subject: Fixing Hunters: 3 Pillars That Would Make Us Legit
content_md:
Look, I love Hunters, been playin em since forever, but let’s be real: on Turtle WoW right now we’re looking like second-class citizens. Pets flop over in raids, Marksman is just sitting there for Trueshot Aura, and Survival? Half the time it dont even know what it wants to be.

 **Beast Mastery**

The Problem: Pets do scale, but it feels weak and underwhelming. BM lost the punch of Bestial Wrath and ended up with a filler ability that does not sell the fantasy or DPS identity.

The Fix:

Stronger Scaling: Pet inherits more of your AP, stamina, and crit. Gearing yourself directly gears your beast in a way that feels impactful.

Pack Leader (new CD): 2 min cooldown. While you and your pet are attacking the same target, both gain +25% damage and +20% attack speed for 12s. Pet heals for 3% of its damage done. This restores the old Bestial Wrath feeling while keeping it synergy-based.

Keeper of Beasts: Unlocks Pet Gear Slots. 3 bonded slots (Collar, Hide, Charm) that act like relics or enchants for pets. Example: Collar = +crit, Hide = +resists, Charm = reduced focus costs. Optional but rewarding for min-maxers.

Capstone Choice:

The Beast Master (burst fantasy): 5 min cooldown. Summons spectral versions of every pet family (cat, wolf, bear, boar, raptor, owl, etc.) for 10s to unleash a flurry of unique attacks. A true “call the pack” moment that delivers BM’s signature burst.

Master of the Pack (raid utility): Unlocks the ability to have two active pets. You must tame and train a second pet from scratch, level it up, and manage both. The second pet deals reduced damage (say 60–70% of a main pet) but brings full utility (Growl, Screech, Howl, etc.). This makes BM more valuable in group content with extra buffs, debuffs, and tanking tools.

End result: BM becomes the definitive pet spec. Stronger scaling makes pets feel rewarding, Pack Leader gives a synergy-based burst window, Keeper of Beasts unlocks deeper customization, and players get to choose between two distinct capstones — flashy burst through ghostly beasts or steady utility with dual companions.

 **Marksman**

The Problem: Marksman feels like a Trueshot Aura bot with clunky burst and weak personal damage. Piercing Shots is especially bad because it forgoes on-the-fly CC — a ticking DoT prevents you from landing Scatter Shot or Freezing Trap setups, leaving you with less control in PvP. The spec also lacks the Ranger identity of using specialized ammunition.

The Fix:

Elemental Quiver (new core mechanic): Buff your arrows like a Rogue uses poisons. Each buff applies to arrow stacks individually, so you must re-apply when swapping types.

Fire Arrows: Add fire damage on hit, with a small AoE splash.

Poison Arrows: Apply a stacking nature DoT.

Frost Arrows: Slow target movement speed, but with a drawback: while Frost Arrows are active, your Aimed Shot and Multi-Shot deal 15% less damage. This makes the snare strong for PvP kiting but balances it against raw DPS.

Replace Piercing Shots: Instead of an uncontrollable DoT, give MM a reactive proc mechanic tied to its signature shots:

Aimed Shot or Multi-Shot crits can reset Concussive Shot’s cooldown or make Serpent Sting instant and free.

Alternatively, procs could make your next Aimed Shot instant but reduced in damage.

This preserves control while rewarding crit-based play.

Double Tap (rework): Passive effect. Auto Shots have a small chance to reset the cooldown of your next ranged ability. This smooths out rotations and avoids clunky on-use stacking.

Capstone Choice:

The Ranger (selfish DPS): Permanently dismiss your pet. Gain +20% ranged attack power, +10% crit chance, and +15% damage on Aimed and Multi-Shot. Aimed Shot crits deal +20% bonus damage.

End result: MM becomes a true Ranger. Elemental Quiver gives ammo depth, Piercing Shots is replaced with a controllable proc system, Frost Arrows have a built-in tradeoff for balance, and you can choose to become a selfish sniper with no pet. PvE gets a competitive DPS option, PvP gets control and versatility without breaking CC balance.

The Problem: Survival is supposed to be the scrappy, dirty-fighting spec, but right now it has no clear identity. Lacerate is clunky and unrealistic since fights aren’t designed around “sides,” and Hunters Mark is wasted when you’re mostly swinging in melee. The tree needs a clearer melee focus with a capstone that feels worth it.

The Fix:

Aspect of the Predator (new stance): Replaces Hawk/Monkey. Reduces ranged weapon range to 16–20 yards and increases melee attack power by +25%. Unlocks Survival-only melee abilities. Cannot be swapped while in combat, forcing commitment.

Weakened Predator (debuff): When you leave Predator, you gain a 15s debuff: -15% melee AP, -15% ranged AP, -10% movement speed. Prevents stance-dancing mid-fight, even with Feign Death.

Hunted Debuff: Replaces Hunters Mark for Survival. Hunted increases all melee damage you deal to the target by 10%. Reinforces your melee playstyle and adds group value.

Raptors Frenzy (new passive): Each time you crit with a melee ability, gain a stack of Raptors Frenzy for 10s (max 3). Each stack increases the damage of your Survival-only melee abilities by 5%. At 3 stacks, your next Survival melee ability also refreshes Hunted. Creates a ramping damage loop that rewards uptime and crit builds.

Hunters Net: 20s cooldown, roots a target in melee for 3s.

Lacerate Rework: Instead of awkward positional damage, becomes a straightforward melee bleed that stacks up to 2 times. Keeps the flavor but makes it functional in real fights.

Capstone — Ambush Predator:

 2 min cooldown. Enter stealth for up to 6s (movement not broken by stealth). Your first melee ability out of stealth stuns the target for 1.5s and applies Hunted, making them take +10% melee damage from you for 6s.

Gives Survival its own assassin-style opener for PvP and PvE, rewarding timing and positioning without being a teleport or leap.

Capstone Choice:

The Beast Master (burst fantasy): 5 min cooldown. Summons spectral versions of every pet family (cat, wolf, bear, boar, raptor, owl, etc.) for 10s to unleash a flurry of unique attacks. A true “call the pack” moment that delivers BM’s signature burst.

author: Dimastasc
subject: Hunter PvP state on Turtle WoW
content_md:
Hi everyone,

I’ve been playing a hunter in PvP on Turtle WoW (patch 1.18), and I wanted to share some thoughts. Right now it feels like hunters are really struggling compared to other classes.

Against Warlocks or Shadow Priests it’s nearly impossible. You can’t escape DoTs, Warlock keeps you under constant control, and hunter’s damage doesn’t pressure them enough before you’re dead.

Paladins and Mages also feel overwhelming: paladins outlast everything, while mages can chain control and burst far harder than hunters can respond.

Hunters lack survival tools — there’s nothing to keep yourself alive or recover once you’re being focused.

At the moment, hunters seem to be at the very bottom in PvP. Maybe instead of buffs, some changes or adjustments could be considered — something to help hunters feel more competitive without breaking balance.

Do other players feel the same, or is it just my experience?

author: Skurridizo
subject: Hunter's redesign and changes after 1.18
content_md:
I made these talents with some changes

[https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/c ... points=F--](https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/calculator?t0=HaEkvLEBZ-&t1=zFMhDOS9rv&t2=ppvJCaxG93&class=4&points=F--)

I'm going to explain the main issues I've seen the hunter has, and how I solved them.

Beast Mastery:

> Pet with low survivability: Buffed and combined Improved Mend Pet + Improved Eyes of the Beast + Improved Revive Pet. Also, there is a new talent providing 2% Vampirism to the pet.
>
>  You have to play Marksman as a second tree and rely on the Steady Shot rotation: Now it’s possible to play BM melee due to some changes in the early Survival talent tree.
>
>  Not much versatility, as there are only 3 useful options for pets: scorpids, wind serpents, or cobras. This isn’t included in the talent tree, but I will detail them later.

Marksmanship:

> Low AoE damage: Spell power buffs for Volley and an extra effect for Scorpid Sting that allows AoE damage.
>
>  Arcane Shot and Aimed Shot are useless: I added a nice combination effect so you can use one of them each time.
>
>  Not many possibilities to combine your talent tree: going deep MM, splashing into BM, or even SV if you want to focus on PvP.
>
>  Not much burst and lacking a real sniper feeling: The new ability Sniper Focus makes your timing and decision-making crucial to when you want to burst.
>
>  Not top DPS nor a supportive spec: Added a new support ability to make it more useful, along with higher-damage talents.

Survival:

> No mobility: Added an extra 5% speed to Lightning Reflexes.
>
>  Bad tree to splash talents into as a secondary tree: Now it’s possible to get +100% extra melee attack power from agility earlier, and another talent reduces minimum range to 0 yards. Feel free to play full melee BM or a hybrid melee-ranged hunter.
>
>  Traps are very clunky in certain situations. In many boss fights, you have to hit at max melee range and lose a large percentage of your total damage: Added a radius expansion for traps if they are not triggered instantly, to increase damage, and also a new mechanic if you want to min/max your traps.

Pet Changes:

> Claw hits 3 targets (like the Druid’s Swipe).
>
>  Claw attack power ratio increased from 1 damage per 42 Attack Power to 1 damage per 35 Attack Power.
>
>  Gorilla’s Thunderstomp cooldown reduced to 10 seconds.

I’m suggesting minor buffs to different identities. Altogether, these changes should allow hunters to match top-tier DPS classes and bring more versatility to both PvE and PvP.

Probably all tiers including 2.5 and above need some changes to scale properly with the 3 specs

author: Lendvell
subject: Re: Hunter's redesign and changes after 1.18
content_md:
Hello, mon. I received your letter with a request to write my comments. I looked at the talent calculator and must say that you did a good job.
Let me share my experience of playing on non-standard hunter builds, as you asked.
 1. I tried to build a viable melee BM. In the current version, his damage was quite average for the following reasons:
 - Due to the fact that 100% agility in MAP is too deep in the survival tree, I had to neglect this talent and collect items not with agility but with AP. Due to the fact that almost all items that enhance your pet, with built-in agility, I greatly lost damage in close combat.
You solved this problem by raising the talent on MAP higher, and also allows you to save talent points on the mandatory Frenzy. And in this build you need a lot of talent points because you need to strengthen not only the pet but also your close combat.

Another big problem with the build is that you don't have good and stable AoE. You tried to solve this problem by adding a 3 targets to the claws and improving the scorpion sting. These are very good changes. However, it is not clear what to do if your pet has a bite, or if you have a talent that applies a serpent sting with attacks, which interrupts the scorpion sting.

 2. I made not bad(I hope) SPD hunter who fights in close combat. Of course, it is weaker than top tier pumping builds, but still not bad. As I understand it, thanks to this build you noticed me.

 - The main problem with SPD hunter (close or ranged) is that there are very few hybrid items that would contain both SP and agility. For some of them you literally have to fight with shamans, because originally, these are their items. And thus you are faced with the problem of lack of damage. You solved this problem by adding a talent to convert part of the RAP into SP.

Overall, you've done a great job. In fact, everything looks so good that I'm starting to think that some of your talents are too strong (for example, the talent that removes the minimum shooting distance)

I hope my experience and my review will be useful to you, and thank you for paying attention to an ordinary player from the server.

Sincerely,
Snakestealer

Adding damage to your next shot can be clunky if it’s applied externally. When you apply it yourself, you control when to start the next attack so you don’t lose the buff. (That’s one of the reasons why I hate the wolf.)

> -Hawk eye, why not just make arcane, serpent and volley scale with ap? Like surv do with traps. Gearing for ap and sp is something I’d hope not to do.

The easiest way to fix all of this is to make your SP scale with your AP. In fact, it’s effectively the same thing, and it allows standard builds to scale their magic damage while also making Spell Power hunters viable for those who enjoy that playstyle.

Lonewolf is against the Classic experience, especially now that pets provide supportive abilities. Moving the hit & weapon skill talent lower in BM would make the pet metagame even more restrictive. Actually I did not boost those abilities as I believed Multi-Shot was fine and Steady-Shot received a boost with the previous patch. I remade the ranged weapon specialization talent to boost our Auto Shot to the level where it was before the class change, where autoshot had dealt more damage than Trueshot(currently Steady Shot). I suggested these changes because I would like to keep and work with what we currently have thanks to Turtle Wow, instead of adding brand new abilities and mechanics from scratch.

This means you can spam this basic rotation for around 2 minutes without running out of mana.
During raids you’ll also have Blessing of Wisdom, increased Spirit and Intellect, and probably a mana regeneration totem.
You can also use mana potions, teas, and mana oil for your melee weapons.

If you want to spam Multishot, Serpent Sting, Arcane Shot, and Baited Shot, obviously you’ll run out of mana and delay your Autoshot animation. You need to think about how to become more efficient instead of playing like a mana powerhouse ready to waste all mana and timing.

But trust me, T2 provides Spirit, T2.5 gives you mana regen with Serpent Sting, T3 gives you a lot of mana, and you also have all the other resources I mentioned above. If you’re having mana issues, you’re playing wrong.
Im playing horde side tel abim. There is no paladin, I dont have seal of wisdom or blessing of wisdom. I run out OOM with steady/ms, with mana pot/tea on CD. Our SV hunters run OOM much quicker, let alone BM.

Since I was inspired, I designed my own tree.

<https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/tree/pOs-Ycfkf5>

The main focus is on big aim shot damage and giving the rotation some breathing room + fix scaling issue by removing clipping for basically all of the endgame content, unless we reach like 30% haste or something crazy.

A skillful skill

content_html:
I made these talents with some changes

https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/c ... points=F--

I'm going to explain the main issues I've seen the hunter has, and how I solved them.

Beast Mastery:
Pet with low survivability: Buffed and combined Improved Mend Pet + Improved Eyes of the Beast + Improved Revive Pet. Also, there is a new talent providing 2% Vampirism to the pet.

You have to play Marksman as a second tree and rely on the Steady Shot rotation: Now it’s possible to play BM melee due to some changes in the early Survival talent tree.

Not much versatility, as there are only 3 useful options for pets: scorpids, wind serpents, or cobras. This isn’t included in the talent tree, but I will detail them later.
Marksmanship:
Low AoE damage: Spell power buffs for Volley and an extra effect for Scorpid Sting that allows AoE damage.

Arcane Shot and Aimed Shot are useless: I added a nice combination effect so you can use one of them each time.

Not many possibilities to combine your talent tree: going deep MM, splashing into BM, or even SV if you want to focus on PvP.

Not much burst and lacking a real sniper feeling: The new ability Sniper Focus makes your timing and decision-making crucial to when you want to burst.

Not top DPS nor a supportive spec: Added a new support ability to make it more useful, along with higher-damage talents.
Survival:
No mobility: Added an extra 5% speed to Lightning Reflexes.

Bad tree to splash talents into as a secondary tree: Now it’s possible to get +100% extra melee attack power from agility earlier, and another talent reduces minimum range to 0 yards. Feel free to play full melee BM or a hybrid melee-ranged hunter.

Traps are very clunky in certain situations. In many boss fights, you have to hit at max melee range and lose a large percentage of your total damage: Added a radius expansion for traps if they are not triggered instantly, to increase damage, and also a new mechanic if you want to min/max your traps.
Pet Changes:
Claw hits 3 targets (like the Druid’s Swipe).

Claw attack power ratio increased from 1 damage per 42 Attack Power to 1 damage per 35 Attack Power.

Gorilla’s Thunderstomp cooldown reduced to 10 seconds.
I’m suggesting minor buffs to different identities. Altogether, these changes should allow hunters to match top-tier DPS classes and bring more versatility to both PvE and PvP.

Probably all tiers including 2.5 and above need some changes to scale properly with the 3 specs

author: Chooze
subject: Re: Hunter's redesign and changes after 1.18
content_md:
Hello, I've been playing survival hunter since 2004 until CATA and it's my favorite class. I'm on Turtle now. I completely forgot how boring hunter is in Vanilla. Almost every class has new abilities from TBC (Shaman: Shields, Shieldblock talents, Totemic Recall / Paladin: Crusader strike, Druid: in 21century doesn't have res, because "vanilla experience" :D ). Hunter is boring autoshot turret!

 **Ideas for improvement:**
 - Deadzone like in TBC
 - **Traps in combat** for all hunters (cd 30s), survival with cd reduction talent.
 - **Steady Shot** for all hunters (increased dmg to dazed targets), maybe stared CD with Arcane?
 - **Aimed Shot** from MM talents: 3rd row, 50% healing reduction, MM talent for casting time reduction after 3x steady, not shared CD with Arcane.
 - More TBC abilities? **Snake trap**, **Misdirection**, **Call Stabled Pet** (quality of life, 5min cd).
 - Rework useless abilities: **Disengage** (maybe something like Ghostly Strike, or parry / dodge, next attack -> synergy with Mongoose Bite and Counterattack). **Distraction shot** (taunt). **Tranquil Shot** (dispel magic, otherrwise useless ability useful in 2 raids).
 - **Mongoose Bite**, every hunter can spam Raptor Strike and Mongoose Bite on CD with nobrain macro. Rework Mongoose, use after parry / dodge (reverse Overpower).
 - **Mana management** - The only DPS class that has problems with mana? -> **Aspect of the Viper** from TBC.
 - Autoshot on right click / Autoattack after enemy comes into melee range

 **Survival:**
 - Should be more of a melee/ranged universal tree than just pure melee.
 - Melee dps without kick/silence? BM has Intimidate, MM has Scatter, SV has nothing, need Wyvern Sleep or Improved Chimaera Strike (more below).
 - **Improved Mongoose Bite** (talent) - can strike after melee critical, melee critical resets CD.
 - Final talent (7th row): Maybe trap CD reduction and more active traps like in WOTLK (frost / fire / nature).
 - Stinging Nettle (talent) - overrides active sting??? -> Lock and Load (WOTLK) or Thrill of the Hunt (TBC): after frost trap / periodic fire dmg has chance to no mana cost for 2 next abilities. (helpful for all specs)
 - **Rework Carve**: Hunter will never be an AOE machine, needs something like Chimaera Strike (3th row, refresh current sting, without aoe, shares CD with Multi, X weapon dmg (maybe strike with both weapons?).
 - **Improved Chimaera Strike**: 5th row talent, Instant nature dmg with Serpent, Dmg reduction or Disarm with Scorpid (inner cd), Instant mana gain or drain with or longer casting time with Viper/ maybe some form of hard CC / synergy with improved stings from MM. Something like Warrior's Master Strike.

 **Beastmasters:**
Swift Aspect, Improved Primal Aspect, Pathfinding, Coordinated Assault - nice synergy with SV
Maybe too many Aspects: Merge Aspect of the Beast with Aspect of the Wolf?

I would try to have each spec have about 2-3 active abilities from talent trees.
BM: Coordinated Assault / Kill Command from TBC, Intimidate, Bestial Wrath
MM: Aimed Shot, Scatter Shot, Trueshot Aura
SV: Deterrence / Chimaera Strike / More active Traps in same time

I am waiting for your reactions.

In this regard, Baited Shot is much more interesting. The only thing I don't like about it is that it is a ranged attack and you have to be a shooter. But I am ready to tolerate this minus.
The concept of "add % of power" only works when there is a hole that needs to be patched. If there is something that works, don't touch it.
In this regard, I really like your approach to redesigning talents. The talent for the combination of arcane shot + aimed shot is pretty good. I don't know how strong it will be, but it looks nice.
The talent for generating power in exchange for time is also nice.
Concept "do X to get Y" is much better and more interesting than "get 9999% power".
Yes, I agree, that would be much better. I just can't see how it would happen. CC2 is done, all we can hope the things we got gets better. Currently hunter is underperforming as a pure damage dealer.

I will still stand by my suggestion for Baited Shot, if you really want to nail down this kind of fantasy you adjust it as such:

 -Make it a small to moderate-radius grenade cast for variable melee/range usage, applying the baited debuff to all it hits
 -Instead of the shot dealing upfront damage, it causes your pet to charge the baited area if in range and do an AoE swipe (think Poison Charge in Naxx but without the dot, this allows your capstone to benefit from +pet damage effects which... really should be a givein)
 -Remove the focus regen aspect to compensate for the AoE component, it's needlessly clunky and pigeonholes us into fast pets for PvE instead of experimenting with Windfury on 1.5 and 2.8 speed ones.

This gives BM cleave damage and on-the-spot pet repositioning, both things they could direly use.

author: Edwanji
subject: One-button Aspect, Hunter's Mark, Pet Attack
content_md:
This took me a bit of work and figuring out APIs, so I figure I'd put it out there in case anybody has a similar Hunter style to mine.
This macro:
 1) If Aspect of the Hawk is not selected, cast Aspect of the Hawk.  I don't know if there's a better way to do this, but I take advantage of Hunter Aspects being stances now.  Basically, if the button for Hawk has the Raven claw texture, it's not activated.
 2) If Hunter's Mark isn't in GCD (likely due to having just cast Aspect of the Hawk) Instruct my pet to attack, and cast Hunter's Mark.

So push once to switch aspect if needed, push again to go on the attack.
Code: Select all

```
/run local t=GetShapeshiftFormInfo(2);if t and strfind(t, "Raven") then CastSpellByName("Aspect of the Hawk");end
/run local c,s=CastSpellByName,"Hunter's Mark";local i=nil;for j=1,180 do local n=GetSpellName(j,BOOKTYPE_SPELL);if n and strfind(n,s) then i=j;break;end end if i then if GetSpellCooldown(i,BOOKTYPE_SPELL)<1 then PetAttack() c(s) end end
```

NOTE: PetAttack() will select the nearest target if you don't have one selected.  That's why it goes before Hunter's Mark.  I'm often too lazy to select the target myself.

author: Dimastasc
subject: Disappointment with BM Hunter at level 40
content_md:
I leveled my Hunter to 40 in the Beast Mastery tree and unlocked the ability “Sausage Shot.” I thought: “Finally, something interesting, a new skill!” But when I tried to use it, the button simply didn’t work. At first, I thought it was a bug, even relogged into the game — but nothing changed.
Then I found out that you can only use it when your pet lands a critical strike. Which means that 99% of the time, the ability is just dead. Basically, it’s an extra button that almost never works.
Honestly, this is the disappointment of the year. An absolutely useless skill that depends on luck instead of player control. With this design, the developers pretty much killed BM Hunter. Thanks for the wasted time… now I have no desire to keep playing.

author: Aronymous
subject: Re: hunter pet
content_md:
Some tips on how it works: You can dismiss a pet while you're not using them, as you probably know.
This comes with a bit of unhappiness if you dismiss them usually, but it's useful to know that you can dismiss them in rest areas without any happiness loss.

Another thing I took a while to realise is that when you feed a pet, they get the "pet fed" status. So when feeding them, you waste food if you feed them many pieces at once. So you ought to wait until the "pet fed" status is gone before feeding another piece.

Maybe you knew those things already, but it took me some time to realise it myself, and once I learned those things, I felt the pet system was more comfortable, as I was not using so much food to keep them happy as I was before.

Another thing that's useful to know is that you can keep 2 pets at the same time even if you only have 1 slot in the stables. You just leave 1 in the stable, train a second one, and if you ever wanted to use the first one again, you can swap their places in the stable. Maybe that was obvious, but it took me a while before I realised I could do it.

So I have two pets who eat different food types. 1 eats meat, another eats fish, fruit, bread and fungus, so that means I can switch out my pet depending on what types of food I have more of at the time.
Meats are always cheap in butchers anyway.

I know this isn't the solution you were asking for, and maybe you knew all of that already, but in case this helps the pet system feel any bit more comfortable, I offer this advice.

author: Azcron
subject: Re: hunter pet
content_md: To gain loyalty requires both xp gained and time spent. Basically, to gain a loyalty level, your pet needs to, no matter what, gain at least 5% of the XP needed for your next level. But there was also a time component on every loyalty level past Unruly. For example, to get to level 4 from level 5, you not only needed the experience gain, but an hour had to pass. This is why sometimes your pet would ding loyalty while you're standing around in town, you had gained the experience, but the time had to pass as well. Always feed your pet and keep them happy. Time requirements are: Rank2 - 0 minutes, Rank3 - 30 minutes, Rank4 - 45 minutes, Rank5 - 60 minutes, and Rank6 - 90 minutes

author: Mekk
subject: Re: hunter pet
content_md:
> **Aronymous wrote: Mon Sep 29, 2025 12:58 pm**
> Another thing I took a while to realise is that when you feed a pet, they get the "pet fed" status. So when feeding them, you waste food if you feed them many pieces at once. So you ought to wait until the "pet fed" status is gone before feeding another piece.

Additionally, if your pet enters combat while the Pet Fed buff is active, it will immediately cancel the effect.  So when you feed your pet, let the buff finish before going into combat.  Also, make sure you are feeding your pet food that is closer to your own level; lower level food does not benefit the pet as much.

Getting a pet from Loyalty 1 (Rebellious) to Loyalty 2 (Unruly) does feel like it takes a long time, and during that initial rank, the Pet can seem like it requires a lot of food, but if you keep the above rules in mind, its really not that bad.

As soon as you tame your pet, when you have a few spare moments, get them up to a Happy state by feeding them one food at a time and letting the buff run its entire duration. If, when you feed them, they reach Happy at the very end of the buff, go ahead and feed them one more time (this should put them a the cap, which will take longer before your next feed).  From that point on, whenever they get Content, take a moment to feed them and let the buff run its full duration.  Once they reach Unruly, their food requirements drop quite a bit; each rank lowers the frequency in which your pet must be fed.  And as Azcron stated, you want to be using them in combat during this time, as you want them gaining XP.

author: Vrag
subject: Please do something about the MM spec
content_md:
Right now I feel like MM is doing less damage than it should and that it is an alpha version of an unfinished class.

My suggestion is to either replace or change ability Aimed shot, because there is literally no reason to use it as an MM Hunter if you can cast 2 steady shots in that casting time of aimed shot that will cause higher damage and you are not risking getting interrupted. I would rather replace it with Kill shot or something else.

Arcane shot is not completely useless but its used as a filler shot. In the early levels it is introduced as a core shot for hunter, but at 60 you are barely using it. Arcane shot does only really weak arcane damage and no physical damage. Please do something with it.

Volley has 1 min cooldown and does a stunning 92 arcane damage, again, no physical damage. Please do something with this.

Trueshot aura is a weird one. You constantly have to put it on in BGs along with the aspect. Why is this toggled? Just make it so its always activated since you put the point in the talent tree.

Serpent Sting - might as well never use it even with the 5/5 talent. The talent is only useful because it increases mana drain of Viper Sting, but barely. The damage it does is terrible.

Disengage - you can rework it to do a leap backwards

The hunter's mark talent is not good

The 2 new talent slots are cool though. The endless quiver makes you bursty at times but the second talent that causes bleeding, I do not notice any change in damage. I would rather that it activates expose weakness or something along those lines, or simply buff the bleeding. But overall this tree is not really interesting and compared to other 2 now it feels unfinished and more often than not, it feels like I am playing an alpha version of the class and some of these abilities are underwhelming and underpowered.

In bgs it feels like I am shooting pebbles at people despite being really good geared with maxed out enchantments and proper rotation. Despite  this, in raids people who have tier 1-2 from other classes can 100% outdps me. How can you then say "MM is in a good spot right now"?. MM Hunters have never been in a worse spot damage wise. People I know who played hunters stopped playing them because of this. I remember hunters doing good damage pre nax and seeing hunters being played by people in general, now I rarely see them.

I main the MM hunter, I love its playstyle but I think these things are an issue and not just for MM hunters, but hunters in general. In PVE its hard to keep up with the damage of other classes, even when you are ultra geared. In PVP I am shooting pebbles at people. Overall, MM hunter is insanely nerfed to oblivion to the point people stopped playing a hunter because of it. Some people don't want to play survival, me included. I will probably be switching to my rogue because why should I torture myself? I think devs shouldn't be afraid to take ideas from TBC or WOTLK in order to make things more interesting. I would love some new abilities or rework of the existing ones.

content_md:
Bestial Wrath should be back and some of the functionality of Baited Shot should be moved somewhere else.

For instance, Kill Command should be a damage attack with a CD that applied a reduced effect of what Baited Shot does now. Bonus points for giving mana back to the hunter if the attack crits.

author: Kerbees
subject: Either the hunter does too little damage or everyone else does too much
content_md:
Thread.

For a damage class, I think we slack a bit too much behind. I don't know if it's normal / because of bugs but we're lacking the numbers for a class that offers nothing but damage and in one spec, a party buff.

But what I really see is that everyone else is doing too much damage. I mean .. everyone has seen at least once a shaman right click someone in PVP into dust just like RNG can (too often, I believe) make Onyxia do a 90°turn to them because they got lucky on the first hit and procced WF+HOJ+WOT cloak. Even if it's fun, it's just a bit too much for them but okay, I digress, this isn't a shaman boohoo thread.

I don't belive it's normal for way too many guilds to mutilate Onyxia and turn her into a handbag in less than a minute with 20 people, maybe that's why I believe everyone does too much damage.

Meanwhile, the hunter has no short CD burst (and rapid fire should increase haste, not just auto shot speed), his damage is cut in half by armor because base damage is so low, the abilities are either still bugged (hello kill command, hello procs, hello so many things) or just plain bad because zero scaling (serpent sting, arcane shot, ROFL volley). The shooting animation makes us too static, multi shot requiring stationary position while it's an "instant" is dumb, the out of combat limitation for traps usage out of the survival spec is dumber, aimed shot is useless, talents offer too little bang for the bucks, our scaling with gear is overall wrong.

This needs to be fixed.

The shooting animation makes us too static, multi shot requiring stationary position while it's an "instant" is dumb, the out of combat limitation for traps usage out of the survival spec is dumber, aimed shot is useless, talents offer too little bang for the bucks, our scaling with gear is overall wrong.

author: Insanefool
subject: Re: Either the hunter does too little damage or everyone else does too much
content_md:
The relatively lower damage output in PvP would be tolerable if it wasn't for the fact that the regular toolkit of scatter shot into freeze trap was nerfed to oblivion. Freeze trap was one of the weaker cc moves from the beginning; easy to resist, easy to break, easy to dispel, easy to miss, requires 3 different spells to cast and land if you are in combat. As you all know the devs nerfed scatter shot with freeze trap to share diminishing returns. meaning your first freeze trap has reduced frozen time after you cast scatter shot. on top of this the rework of the survival tree actually nerfed the fuck out of freeze trap even further. Freeze trap was arguably YOUR MOST IMPORTANT PVP TOOL. The diminishing returns change alone sent hunters from one of the worst classes in PvP to the absolute worst class in PvP.

The class was essentially ruined at that point but also on top of that they added a cooldown to wingclip for no fucking reason, completing the circle of giving the hunters no ability to reliably peel. So now if melee parries or blocks your wing clip spell you are boned. Its a total shit show.

Really, melee hunter shouldn't even exist. Is it supposed to funny? Whats funny about it? I remain competitive as marksman hunter because im BIS and ive played hunter forever, but when matched against other high skill PvP veterans I need luck and prayers now. By comparison playing hunter in TBC is infinitely more fun. As a survival hunter in TBC you can truly manage 1v3s against other fully geared players by maximizing your toolkit. I cant begin to tell you how fun and interesting those crazy match ups can be. On turtle wow when you play survival hunter the whole play style appears to be suicide dive-bombing into everything.

author: Allwynd01
subject: Re: Either the hunter does too little damage or everyone else does too much
content_md:
I find it hard to believe that every class is a really good DPS or they should be. I think this comes from the mentality that more DPS = more viability, but in reality it's an RPG so some classes should be good at things that others aren't.

I don't think a Priest can be the best DPS as it's mostly developed around healing, just like how a Rogue or a Hunter can't be a good healer.

So in RPG philosophy, I think each class should be good at something that others aren't so they can compensate each other when in a group. Otherwise it's just homogenizing all classes like Retail where there is no difference between them.

In my opinion Hunter should have CC abilities that immobilize and impede enemies so the DPS classes can do their job. And it's a mistake to think a Hunter should be a DPS monster just because he can shoot or has a pet. I think the idea for Hunter was the pet most of all - your pet does melee while you stand back and shoot and use traps and shots.

author: Jinxes
subject: Re: Either the hunter does too little damage or everyone else does too much
content_md:
I don't know about the other specs, but something is definitely wrong with MM hunter.

As a MM hunter, I'm consistently getting out-DPS'd by other classes several levels below me and in green questing gear (this was a problem in leveling dungeons too, but I wrongly assumed that would go away at level 60). I have tried for weeks to figure out what I'm doing wrong, from gear choices to spec choices to rotation choices, but to no avail. I have started to wonder whether my DPS tracker is just bugged or if there's a bug in damage output somehow.

I've gotten some help with this from my guild, and while they're still happy to bring me to raids for my toolkit, it's very demotivating to notice that I'm really not pulling my weight like other classes are able to. It's even worse in PvP, where concussive shot seems to be my only consistently meaningful contribution.

Ignoring aimed shot, arcane shot, and all of my stings, is about the only thing that has improved my damage output somewhat in PvE. Trash mobs go down too fast for Hunter's Mark to contribute any meaningful damage, instead just sapping my mana. Volley and multishot move the needle a bit, but only situationally, if the conditions are exactly right. Better ammo helps, but not enough to justify the cost.

At this point, I may as well have nothing but steady shot on my bar, which is very unsatisfying and disappointing. I would like for my other abilities to also be meaningful.

I'm not quite sure exactly how to fix any of this, but it's clear to me that MM hunters need a baseline boost to DPS *somehow*, and rebalanced values between different types of shots.

And, quite frankly, I would love for MM to have the option to not use a pet at all, in exchange for a boost to damage, similar like Soul Entrapment for demonology warlocks.

I made a draft of change ideas here (highlighted changed or moved talents):
<https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/tree/CAp1KrlflY>

I am not saying it is perfectly balanced, but tried to give answers to most problems I've seen with MM within the tree itself.

Changes:
 * Scatter Shot moved up. I think it could be allowed to a non-OP PVP build to have an easier access to the shot if wanted.
 * Improved Hunter's Mark, Barrage and Mortal Shots: reduced the TP requirement. Also, added Volley ranged attack power scaling within the Barrage talent.
 * Improved Steady Shot: gave it an armor penetration debuff made by ranged attacks to help hunters against high armor opponents.
 * Endless Quiver: Hid a bit of mana engine here: 'This additional shot does not spend ammo and regenerates 1/2% of your mana.'
 * Trueshot Aura: This might be overdoing it but as an idea I noted it. Aura's effect doubling for ranged attack power.
 * Lone Wolf: If you pay a TP and don't use a pet, you get 2% crit and 1 sec smaller CDs on each marksmanship talents. Again, can be probably fine-tuned for balance but I think this is an interesting idea to generally go with it.

author: Kullez
subject: Proposed Improvements for the Marksmanship Hunter
content_md:
**Good day!**
I play a Hunter on our server and greatly enjoy the changes you’ve made to the Beast Mastery and Survival specializations. Although the recent rebalance of Marksmanship—my long-time favorite—has been positive, I feel that these adjustments don’t fully reflect the “core identity” of the MM specialization, which I will explain below. With that in mind, I would like to propose several ideas that could improve the gameplay experience for Marksmanship Hunters. These are merely suggestions, but I would be genuinely thrilled to see them implemented:

 **TALENT REWORKS:**

 1. (First option — depending on the balancing of the new talent *Ensnaring Net*, described below)
Change the talent *Improved Concussive Shot* with the following:
(x/5 points) Extends the duration of *Concussive Shot* by 0.4 seconds per point and adds a 2% chance per point (up to 10%) to entangle the target in a net for 5 seconds, preventing movement.

 2. (Second option — depending on the balancing of the new talent *Ensnaring Net*, described below)
Change the talent *Improved Concussive Shot* with the following:
(x/5 points) Extends the duration of *Concussive Shot* by 0.4 seconds per point.

 3. (If introducing 1/2 or 2/2 variants proposed below)
Change the talent *Endless Quiver* with the following:
(x/1 point) Your *Auto Shot*, *Stready Shot*, *Arcane Shot* and *Multi-Shot* have a 5% chance to fire an additional shot that does not consume ammunition and deals 100% weapon damage.

 4. (If introducing 1/2 or 2/2 variants proposed below)
Change the talent *Improved Steady Shot* with the following:
(x/1 point) Increases the damage of *Steady Shot* by 12.5%.

 **NEW TALENTS:**

 1. (First option) *Lone Wolf*
x/1 talent point, available after spending 30 points in the Marksmanship tree.
Effect: If you do not have a pet summoned, you gain the *Lone Wolf* buff, increasing all damage dealt by 10/12.5/15% (depending on the rank of the ability).

 2. (Second option) *Lone Wolf*
x/1 talent point, available after spending 30 points in the Marksmanship tree.
Effect: You can no longer summon a pet, permanently gaining the *Lone Wolf* buff, which increases all damage dealt by 10/12.5/15% (depending on the rank of the ability).

 3. (First option) *Ensnaring Net*
Available after spending 30 points in the Marksmanship tree, x/1 talent point.
Deals no damage. Cooldown: 30 seconds. Requires the *Lone Wolf* buff to use.
(Optional: Add a consumable for its activation — *Hunter’s Net*, purchased at the same vendors as arrows, bullets, and water. Cost: 50 copper, stack size: 100.)
PvE Effect (vs mobs or adds): 100% chance to entangle any creature except dragonkin and giants, preventing movement for 10 seconds. Against giants: 50% chance; against dragonkin: 75%. Does not work on elite mobs or bosses.
PvP Effect (vs players): 100% chance to immobilize players for 5 seconds. Counts as a root effect and can be removed.

 **WHY?**

Hunters have three specializations:
 *Beast Mastery* is structured so that the Hunter primarily empowers the pet—roughly a 70/30 distribution, where the pet deals the majority of the impact.
 *Survival* focuses on close-range combat with heavy use of traps, while the pet provides meaningful assistance—roughly 65/35, with the Hunter leading the damage.
 *Marksmanship*, described as masters of precision, ranged combat, and powerful shots, still relies considerably on the pet—around 75/25, even though the Hunter is intended to be the main source of damage.

Across various servers and expansions (except TBC), up to Legion, my main character has always been a Marksmanship Hunter. Because of this, I would love to see a version of the Legion-style talent that prevents pet summoning entirely. I enjoy using a pet, but sometimes I want to play as a ranger or archer similar to elven bowmen—and they traditionally do not use animal companions, yet are still recognized as archers.

With the addition of new control options, an increased duration for *Concussive Shot*, and overall higher outgoing damage, Marksmanship Hunters would find it far more manageable to operate without a pet. I haven’t yet participated in raids on this server, so I cannot confidently judge the exact percentage values for *Lone Wolf* or related effects, but I sincerely ask you to consider my proposal. I hope that with one of the upcoming patches, I will be able to dismiss my pet entirely and fully embrace a playstyle centered on the Hunter’s own capabilities.

Have a nice day!

author: Calli
subject: Re: Proposed Improvements for the Marksmanship Hunter
content_md:
Arcane Shot should be buffed to deal more damage—or at least equal damage to Steady Shot—by allowing it to scale from attack power, similar to Survival traps. This would make our rotation less boring and give us an option to use while moving. If that change causes issues in PvP, the ability could be adjusted so that 50% of its damage is dealt instantly and the other half applied as a 6-second DoT (5 seconds if talented). This way, crowd control could not be combined with it in PvP.

Serpent Sting could be improved by adding a debuff that has an X% chance to proc from the DoT. When this effect procs on the target, that would signal the right time to use Aimed Shot. Aimed Shot would retain its 3-second cast time but deliver very strong damage to make the risk of casting it worthwhile.

Trueshot Aura should grant X melee attack power and 2X ranged attack power to compensate for the fact that Blessing of Might and Battle Shout provide zero ranged attack power.

These changes could be implemented quite easily by simply adjusting a few numbers.

I support the Lone Wolf concept, but it should deal less damage than using a pet, since the micro-management of a pet should be rewarded. However, the option would still be available for players who prefer to play without their companion.

Hello!
The whole point of *Steady Shot* is that the requirement to cast it is rewarded with higher damage. I support the idea of a small buff to *Arcane Shot*, but I think its damage should not exceed 80% of the total damage dealt by *Steady Shot* over a full rotation. As for PvP—the proposed control improvements together with the *Arcane Shot* buff (through talents) are already quite significant. I don’t think that with a 5-second cooldown there’s any need for a damage split or a 50/50 mechanic.

Regarding *Aimed Shot*, I agree, though tying it to a DoT is debatable. It might be better to consider a “balancing” approach: make its base cast time 4 seconds, but allow it to fire as a guaranteed critical (with half the cast time—2 seconds) after *Piercing Shot* procs. It’s also a DoT, but tied to the MM specialization. If the goal is to make this work for “all” hunters, then the Serpent Sting DoT proc chance should be no higher than two percent because of the constant ticking damage on the target.

As for *Trueshot Aura*, I don’t see much reason to increase melee damage for the MM tree. Instead, perhaps it could give a one/two percent temporary buff when traps trigger on an enemy (as a temporary bonus for Survival), though I won’t speak for the Survival spec.

Regarding *Lone Wolf*, I believe that playing with or without a pet should offer equally valuable rewards. Running Heroics as MM, I simply wouldn’t have managed without a pet. Based on that, I proposed the control adjustments—so there would be a chance to survive on your own while dealing damage from range.

So the ideas are very good; they’re definitely worth considering.

Hello! Regarding the idea of buffing *Serpent Sting* — up to 600 damage over its duration sounds rather low; however, for MM it would be worth working on the *Piercing Shot*  effect. Granting armor penetration is a good idea, but it depends on how it’s implemented. If considered as a global armor reduction, it would provide a bonus to the entire group/raid. In that case, the number of such debuffs should be limited to 1–2; otherwise, the damage would be too strong (I suggest refreshing and replacing the debuff when there are 3 or more hunters). If, on the other hand, it remains the current (solo) effect, then the bonus should be scaled proportionally, with scaling based on attack power.

In general, *Serpent Sting* could be weakened in its base version, with the emphasis shifted toward a permanent *Lone Wolf* buff — for example, the solo effect described above could only apply while this buff is active. This doesn’t seem particularly difficult to implement in code.

As for *Serpent Sting* overall, it’s a debatable topic. The Survival tree already has a final talent that effectively provides a “buff without a buff” (the one that allows placing traps in combat) — similarly, it could allow using *Serpent Sting* ONLY at close range (melee distance, as at BFA). For BM, it could be tied to the pet in some way… but that’s for you to decide. At this point, it’s more in the realm of speculation.

author: Vrag
subject: MM hunter fixes devs should focus on
content_md:
I think you devs should really focus on ranged hunter. In one of the previous patches you guys said MM is in good spot right now but I disagree and from the ton of posts I see, that doesn't seem to be the case. I can top the leaderboards in battlegrounds and can kill people 1v1 but it requires of me to really try really hard and use every trick I can think of. I also play a warlock and I do not have the same feeling and issues with that class that I have with hunter.

Aimed shot in pvp is 90% useless in pvp even in pve. You can use it to start the fight but beyond that its useless and has long wind up time, has no guaranteed crit and in majority of cases you are better off doing auto shot and steady shot and it will deal more damage. Many here have good ideas for aimed shot, to make it proccable, to make it a guaranteed critical hit etc. Anything will be better than what we have now.

Serpent sting with maxed out talent deals such a low damage that its crazy. Not to mention that talent needs 5 points to still deal that low damage. This damage should be increased and that talent slot should cost 2 talent points not 5.

Arcane shot deals max 183 damage, no attack power just pure arcane damage that low. It needs attack power boost or something

Volley same thing as arcane shot. AoE that does low damage with huge cooldown.

Winged clip if you are playing MM hunter has a 3sec cooldown which is terrible in PVP. I understand they did that because they overhauled survival tree but they screwed over MM hunters in pvp hard with that because getting melee opponents out of your deadzone is a gamble. They also removed counterattack, a proccable melee stun that procs on parry. This ability was good if you were MM playing battlegrounds to get away from attackers, but it was removed.

Trueshot aura being the final talent ability in the tree is also insane to me. Meanwhile warlock gets dark harvest, most damaging death ray ability and we get a weak aura? Replace trueshot aura with some ultimate shot ability.

These are all issues the majority of ranged hunters on turtlewow agree should be looked at.
I play MM as a sort of ninja ranged acrobat but I miss the abilities to add to rotations. Its genuinely sad that this class is reduced to autoattack, steady shot and multishot combos. I still use these abilities when I find it appropriate but that its underwhelming is an understatement.

Also, rogues now can kill you really quick. With the addition of Sweet n Crunchy Fruit Bread they pop that and you can't freeze them to get away. Even when you find opening to get away with scatter shot, you still have slow poison on you. You can deploy frost trap fd combo but rogue bypasses that with sprint. Your only option then is to use anti venom but rogue can range attack you with slow and again apply slow poison. In that case you can't use anti venom again because it has a cooldown but then again you are relying on first aid to do that. Wing clip nerf and removal of counterattack in this case is a further salt on the wound. I do not want rogues nerfed but what I am saying is that ranged hunters now have significantly reduced means of escaping. We already have big deadzone which in TBC was severely reduced and all these reductions in melee CC makes it impossible to get away. Warriors also, pretty similar situation in fights with them.

author: Kullez
subject: Refoged Rhok'Delar - as legendary hunter weapon
content_md:
Hi guys,
yesterday at night I was thinking about a possible hunter legendary weapon and came up with this idea.
(yes, you can say “this is Legion chiiiild, wth”, and I’m not a Turtle WoW lore specialist, but hear me out):

 ***Questline concept:***
 **Corrupted Rhok’Delar** → **Sealed Rhok’Delar** → **Reforged Rhok’Delar, Bow of the Dragon Aspirant**
Yeah, I want to make a legendary weapon from Rhok’Delar, because I like it.

 ***Questline overview***
A corrupted boss (Old Gods/Legion/Nightmare-related) is added to the Timbermaw Hold raid.
After killing it, Hunters can obtain a legendary quest item (tentacle / heart with a 20% drop chance). ***1st step.***
Taking the quest requires equipping Rhok’Delar. Upon completion, Rhok’Delar transforms into **Corrupted Rhok’Delar**.

 **Corrupted Rhok’Delar**:
 1. damage somewhere around Naxxramas bows (≈60 DPS)
 2. each shot drains 25–50 HP from the Hunter
 3. each shot has a 2–3% chance to stun the Hunter for 3 seconds, causing total loss of control while standing in place. This stun cannot be dispelled or resisted
 4. the corruption effect remains on the weapon until it is sealed later in the questline
Quest text describes the bow as literally rotting and decaying, with the Hunter fearing it may eventually crumble in their hands (can be removed).

 ***2nd step: C’Thun and the Emerald Dream***
The next step requires defeating C’Thun, only if the Hunter is Exalted with the Brood of Nozdormu and has **Corrupted Rhok’Delar** equipped (during the entire C’Thun fight).

Details:
 1. upon entering Ahn’Qiraj, C’Thun whispers to the Hunter, and the bow starts whispering too.
 2. after defeating C’Thun, the Hunter can speak with an Avatar of C’Thun, who reveals that the corrupted boss was merely a pawn (Old Gods/Legion/Nightmare — pick one).
 3. their goal was to reach the power of the Emerald Dream using an ancient weapon infused with corruption
After the conversation, the Hunter is suddenly pulled into the Emerald Dream, where they meet an Avatar of Ysera.
Ysera initially threatens to destroy both the Hunter and the weapon. However, seeing the Hunter’s role in defeating C’Thun (reputation requirement), she instead decides to help.

She transforms the weapon into **Sealed Rhok’Delar**:
 1. power level slightly above a standard “T2” weapon (≈45 DPS).
 2. grants an Emerald Blessing bonus (see final weapon effects).
 3. maybe some pet bonuses, idk.
 4. all negative corruption effects are removed, but there is a 1% chance to break the weapon in combat.

 ***Reforging process (3rd step)***
To fully reforge the bow, the Hunter must gather dragon-related components:
 1. **Azuregos sinew** (or an instanced / summoned version without non-quest loot, because of world boss issues on Nordanaar) — provides the bowstring
 2. **Emerald Dragon Scale** for one of the four green dragon world bosses (or instanced equivalents)/Solnius from the Emerald Sanctum — provides purified scales for the bow’s frame.
 3. **Heart of Nefarian** (for “negative” balance and power source)
 4. **Blessing of Anachronos** (requires Exalted with the Brood of Nozdormu, to balance all power and stabilize the bow) - from dialog with Anachronos.

 ***4th step (final)***] after bringing all components to Ysera and receiving her blessing, the Hunter receives:
 **The title “Defender of the Emerald Dream” or “Dragon Aspirant”**
 **Reforged Rhok’Delar, Bow of the Dragon Aspirant**

 ***WEAPON:***
 **Reforged Rhok’Delar, Bow of the Dragon Aspirant**
Weapon type: Bow (Ranged)
Quality: Legendary
(Cannot be sold, deleted, or traded. Can be stored in the bank.)
Ammo: Arrows
Class: Hunter only (MM-oriented, but still good for other specs)

 **Stats**
+15 Agility
+25 Stamina
+15 Strength

Speed: 3.10
Damage: 228,3 – 268,5
DPS: ~80.1

Durability: 250 / 250
(or infinite, explained as the Green Dragonflight continuously restoring the bow)

 **Effects**
Equip: +2% Hit Chance
Equip: +2% Critical Strike Chance

Equip: **Blessing of Anachronos**
After five successful Stready Shots, your next Aimed Shot becomes instant.
Internal cooldown: 15 seconds
Mana cost is consumed, ammo is not consumed.

Equip: Chance on any attack (3%) to trigger one of the following effects
Internal cooldown: 24 seconds (starts when an effect triggers); the same effect cannot occur twice in a row; can trigger from any combat ability (including Mongoose Bite, Kill Command, Arcane Shot)

 **Emerald Blessing**: for 8 seconds, abilities cost no mana and heal the Hunter for 5% of damage dealt
 **Black Dragonflight’s Fury**: increases melee and ranged attack power by 150 for 6 seconds

Active ability:
 **Magic of the Blue Dragonflight**
Creates 200 “Blue Dragonflight Arrows”

 **Blue Dragonflight Arrows**: arrow damage 24; soulbound; cannot be sold, traded, or banked
Cooldown: 6 hours

I really want to see something like this. Right now I’m only an AQ40 raider, but believe me, I can earn this bow.
Numbers and mechanics are obviously adjustable — the main goal is to provide Hunters with a true legendary progression, because I want it aaaand an instant Aimed Shot (if a talent for it is added, the effect can trigger a new talent proc, but with a 30 sec cooldown).

author: Atreidon
subject: Re: Hunter mana issues are pervasive across ALL levels, not just levels 56-60.
content_md:
Hunter is a martial class. While levelling they have really good dps output from just autoshots and their pet doing the heavy lifting. This is intentional.

Your spells comparatively are not adding that much damage for a somewhat pricy bit for your manapool.

But you aren't a pure caster class. You can simply wear a bit of spirit gear and shoot the occasional baddy without the use of spells to just regain the mana. Playing hunter is a lesson in understanding the 5 second rule. Every time you pay mana, for the next seconds you will not regain any mana (except for mp5)

So bundle your spells into bursts, and then just use your potent autoattacks for a bit when you need to regen.
